lessons.name: Primitive Types & Type Inference
lessons.desc: TypeScript infers types automatically from values. The type system is structural. Const infers literal types; let infers widened types.
lessons.q: What is the difference between type inference and explicit annotation? When does TypeScript infer the wrong type and you must annotate explicitly?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between let x = 5 (inferred as number) and const x = 5 (inferred as literal 5)? Why does that matter for unions?
terms: TypeScript khud samajh leta hai ki value kis type ki hai — aapko likhna nahi padta.
let ke saath type chauda ho jaata hai — "hi" se string ban jaata hai.
Type jo sirf ek hi value allow kare — jaise "hi".
lessons.what:
TypeScript zyadatar type khud pehchan leta hai. const x = 5 likhne par usko pata hai ki ye number hai — : number likhne ki zarurat nahi.

Par ek chhota farak hai: const se type bilkul wahi value banti hai, aur let se type chauda ho jaata hai.
lessons.why: Har jagah type likhna TypeScript ka maqsad nahi hai. Jitna kam likhoge utna code saaf rahega. Type wahan likho jahan wo ek contract ho — function ke arguments, return type, aur exported cheezein. Andar ke variables inference par chhod do.

const arr = [] ka type never[] ban jaata hai — const arr: string[] = [] likho.

lessons.name: type vs interface
lessons.desc: Both describe object shapes. interface supports declaration merging and is open for extension. type is more flexible — supports unions, intersections, tuples, and mapped types.
lessons.q: When would you use type over interface and vice versa? What is declaration merging and when is it useful or dangerous?
lessons.qsub: Can a type extend an interface? Can an interface extend a type? Show both syntaxes and explain the subtle differences in behaviour.
terms: Object ka naksha. Dobara declare karne par merge ho jaata hai.
Kisi bhi type ko naam dena — union, primitive, function, object.
Do ek naam ke interface apne aap jud jaate hain.
lessons.what:
90% cases mein dono ek jaise hain. Do asli farak hain:

1. type kuch bhi naam de sakta hai — union, primitive, tuple. interface sirf object shape.
2. interface ek hi naam se dobara likhne par merge ho jaata hai. type error deta hai.
lessons.why: Wahi merging jo library authors ke liye feature hai (aap third-party types mein apna field jod sakte ho), aapke apne code mein bug hai — do jagah same naam likh diya aur pata hi nahi chala.

visual.cap: Ek hi sawaal se faisla: "kya main sirf object ka shape bana raha hu?" Haan to dono chalte hain; nahi to type hi option hai.

lessons.name: Union & Intersection Types
lessons.desc: Union (A | B): the value can be either type. Intersection (A & B): the value must satisfy both types simultaneously.
lessons.q: Explain union vs intersection with real examples. When does an intersection type produce never and why?
lessons.qsub: Draw the mental Venn diagram. Why does an intersection of {a:string} & {a:number} produce {a:never} instead of a valid type?
terms: "Ya to ye, ya wo" — dono mein se koi ek.
"Ye bhi aur wo bhi" — dono ek saath.
Union mein se ek type tak pahunchna, check laga kar.
lessons.what:
| aur & ka matlab ulta lagta hai, aur yahi sabse aam confusion hai.

A | B = value A ya B ho sakti hai. Isliye aap sirf wahi use kar sakte ho jo dono mein ho — kam properties.
A & B = value mein A aur B dono ke fields hain. Zyada properties.
lessons.analogy: Union = "chai ya coffee" — pakka nahi kaunsi, to aap sirf wo maang sakte ho jo dono mein ho (garam hai kya?). Intersection = "chai wali coffee" — dono ki khoobiyan ek saath.
lessons.why: Union hi wo cheez hai jisse TypeScript "ye teen haalatein ho sakti hain" model karta hai — loading / success / error, ya alag-alag event types. Aur uske saath narrowing (agla topic) hi wo tarika hai jisse aap safely un haalaton ko handle karte ho.

visual.cap: Union mein value ek hi type ki hai (par pata nahi kaunsi), isliye common properties hi mil sakti hain. Intersection mein dono ke fields ek saath.

Success aur failure ke alag-alag shapes.
pros: Asambhav haalatein likhi hi nahi ja sakti.
Intersection se props merge karna ek line ka kaam.
Compiler har case handle karwata hai (exhaustive check).
cons: Union par kuch bhi use karne se pehle narrow karna padta hai.
Bade unions ke error messages bahut lambe ho jaate hain.
| aur & ka matlab ulta lagta hai.
gotchas: Union se kam properties milti hain, intersection se zyada — ye ulta lagta hai par sochne par sahi hai.
Do primitives ka intersection never hota hai — koi value dono nahi ho sakti.
Union ke members mein ek common literal field rakho (status) — usse narrowing bahut aasan ho jaati hai.

lessons.name: Literal Types & const Assertions
lessons.desc: Literal types narrow a type to an exact value (e.g. "GET"). as const freezes an object's inferred types to their literal values, preventing widening.
lessons.q: What is a literal type? What does as const do that a regular type annotation cannot? Why is it crucial for arrays used as tuples?
lessons.qsub: Why does TypeScript infer string for let but "hello" for const? What is type widening and when does it cause subtle bugs?
terms: Type jo sirf ek hi value allow kare — "up", 42, true.
Poori cheez ko literal types mein lock kar do — object aur array bhi.
lessons.what:
Ek type jo sirf ek value allow karta hai. Akele bekaar lagta hai, par union ke saath ye TypeScript ka sabse kaam ka feature ban jaata hai.

"small" | "medium" | "large" — ab chauthi value likhi hi nahi ja sakti, aur editor teeno suggest karta hai.
lessons.why: Plain string se typo pakda hi nahi jaata — "smal" bhi ek valid string hai. Literal union se wo galti likhte waqt pakdi jaati hai, chalte waqt nahi.
where: variant: "primary" | "danger" — galat value likhi hi nahi ja sakti.
as const se poora config object type-safe.
typeof ARR[number] — list aur type ek hi jagah se.
pros: Typo likhte waqt pakda jaata hai.
Editor saare valid options suggest karta hai.
typeof ARR[number] se list aur type kabhi alag nahi hote.
cons: as const sab kuch readonly bana deta hai — kabhi-kabhi wo problem hai.
let ke saath widening har baar yaad rakhni padti hai.
Bahut bade unions ke error messages bhaari ho jaate hain.
gotchas: as const deep hai — nested objects bhi readonly ho jaate hain. Agar aage push karna hai to problem aayegi.
const SIZES = [...] as const + typeof SIZES[number] — ye pattern yaad kar lo, roz kaam aayega.
Object property inference se widen ho jaati hai — { mode: "dark" } ka mode string hai jab tak as const na ho.

lessons.name: Type Narrowing & Control Flow
lessons.desc: TypeScript refines a union type to a narrower type inside conditional blocks using control-flow analysis — typeof, instanceof, in, equality checks, and type predicates.
lessons.q: List all the ways to narrow a type in TypeScript. What is a type predicate (is) and when do you need one vs relying on built-in narrowing?
lessons.qsub: What is a discriminated union? How does TypeScript use the literal discriminant to narrow in a switch? What does never tell you at the end of a switch?
terms: Union se ek specific type tak pahunchna, check laga kar.
TypeScript ka aapke if ko padh kar type ka andaza lagana.
Wo common field jiski value se pata chale ki kaunsa member hai.
lessons.what:
TypeScript aapke if ko padhta hai. if (typeof x === "string") ke andar wo jaanta hai ki x string hai — aap x.toUpperCase() likh sakte ho.

Ise control flow analysis kehte hain, aur ye TypeScript ka sabse smart hissa hai.
lessons.why: Union safe hai par akela bekaar — usme se kuch use karne ke liye pehle ye pata karna padta hai ki kaunsa member hai. Narrowing wahi karta hai, bina as lagaye. Aur as se bachna hi asli faayda hai, kyunki as compiler ko chup karata hai, galti theek nahi karta.

pros: as lagaye bina type safe ho jaata hai.
Switch par exhaustive check milta hai — naya case bhoolna namumkin.
Normal JavaScript checks se hi kaam ho jaata hai.
cons: Callback ya async ke andar narrowing toot jaati hai.
Function call ke baad TS maan leta hai ki cheez badal sakti hai.
Complex conditions mein hamesha kaam nahi karta.
gotchas: Callback ke andar narrowing toot jaati hai — kyunki TS ko nahi pata wo kab chalega. Local const mein copy le lo.
typeof null === "object" — pehle x === null check karo.
Union ke har member mein ek common literal field (kind/status) rakho. Wahi narrowing ko aasan banata hai.

lessons.name: strictNullChecks & Nullability
lessons.desc: With strictNullChecks on, null and undefined are their own distinct types — you must explicitly handle them. The non-null assertion (!) removes them unsafely.
lessons.q: What changes when you enable strictNullChecks? Explain the non-null assertion operator (!) and when it is a code smell vs genuinely necessary.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between optional property a?: string (string | undefined) and a: string | null? When does it matter?
terms: TS ka wo flag jo null/undefined ko alag types maanta hai.
"Main kasam khata hu ye null nahi hai" — compiler chup ho jaata hai.
Field ho bhi sakta hai, na bhi ho.
lessons.what:
Bina strictNullChecks ke null har type mein chhupa baithta hai — string ka matlab "string ya null" ho jaata hai, aur TypeScript aapko bacha nahi paata.

Iske saath null aur undefined apne alag types ban jaate hain, aur unhe handle kiye bina aage badha hi nahi ja sakta.
lessons.why: "Cannot read properties of undefined" JavaScript ka sabse aam crash hai. strictNullChecks ek hi flag se us poori class ke bugs ko chalne se pehle pakad leta hai. Ye TypeScript ka sabse zyada faayda dene wala flag hai — isliye strict: true hamesha on.
where: strict: true se ye apne aap on hota hai.
Optional fields ko honestly ? se mark karo.
pros: JavaScript ka sabse aam crash chalne se pehle pakda jaata hai.
?. aur ?? se handle karna chhota rehta hai.
Code padh kar pata chalta hai ki kya missing ho sakta hai.
cons: Purane codebase mein on karne par sau errors ek saath aate hain.
Log ! laga kar chup kara dete hain — jo poora point khatam kar deta hai.
Kabhi-kabhi check likhna padta hai jahan aap jaante ho value hai.
gotchas: ! compiler ko chup karata hai, bug theek nahi karta. Har ! ek jagah hai jahan chalte waqt crash ho sakta hai.
x?: number aur x: number | undefined alag hain — pehle mein field gayab ho sakta hai.
Purane project mein migrate karte waqt file-by-file on karo, poora ek saath nahi.

lessons.name: Enums vs const enum vs Union Types
lessons.desc: Regular enums generate a runtime JS object. const enums are erased at compile time (inlined). String literal unions are the modern, zero-runtime alternative.
lessons.q: What is the difference between a regular enum, const enum, and a string literal union? Why do many teams prefer union types over enums?
lessons.qsub: What is the enum isolation problem with const enum across module boundaries? Why does isolatedModules forbid const enums from external modules?
terms: Naam wale constants ka group — chalte waqt ek asli object banta hai.
Wahi, par compile hote waqt values inline ho jaati hain.
lessons.what:
enum aisa lagta hai jaise TypeScript ka natural feature hai — par ye un chand cheezon mein se hai jo chalte waqt asli JavaScript code banati hain. Baaki poora type system compile ke baad gayab ho jaata hai; enum nahi hota.

Aur zyadatar cases mein ek simple literal union wahi kaam behtar kar deta hai.
lessons.why:
Enum ke teen chhupe hue nuksaan hain: wo bundle mein extra code jodta hai, numeric enum type-safe hai hi nahi (koi bhi number chala jaata hai), aur wo TypeScript-only hai — plain JS se import karne par ajeeb behave karta hai.

Isliye aaj ki salah: default union use karo, enum tab jab sach mein reverse mapping chahiye.

lessons.name: Structural Typing & Excess Property Checks
lessons.desc: TypeScript checks shape compatibility, not nominal identity. Excess property checking only applies to fresh object literals — not to variables already typed.
lessons.q: What is structural typing and how does it differ from nominal typing? What is excess property checking and why does it only apply to object literals?
lessons.qsub: How can you bypass excess property checking (variable assignment, as, satisfies)? When is bypassing it intentional vs a bug?
terms: Type match hota hai shape se, naam se nahi.
Type match hota hai naam se — Java/C# ka tarika. TS mein nahi.
Object literal seedha assign karne par extra fields par error.
lessons.what: TypeScript ye nahi dekhta ki type ka naam kya hai — wo dekhta hai ki uska shape match karta hai ya nahi. Agar object mein zaroori fields hain, to wo us type ka maana jaayega, chahe usne kabhi us interface ka naam bhi na suna ho.
lessons.analogy: Duck typing: "agar wo duck jaisi chalti hai aur duck jaisi bolti hai, to wo duck hai." Naam se koi matlab nahi, behaviour se hai.
lessons.why: Isi wajah se aap third-party objects apne functions ko de sakte ho bina unhe badle. Par iska ek nuksaan bhi hai: UserId aur PostId dono string hain, to TypeScript unhe ek hi cheez maanta hai — aur galat id pass karna pakda nahi jaata. (Uska ilaaj "branded types" hai.)
where: Bina badle apne functions ko de sakte ho.
Sirf zaroori fields maango, poora object nahi.
Jab do same-shape cheezein alag honi chahiye.
pros: Flexible — objects ko interface implement karne ki zarurat nahi.
Third-party code ke saath aasani se chalta hai.
Testing mein nakli object banana bahut aasan.
cons: Same shape wali alag cheezein interchangeable ho jaati hain (UserId vs PostId).
Excess property check ke niyam shuru mein ajeeb lagte hain.
Nominal typing ke liye jugaad (branding) karna padta hai.
gotchas: Excess property check sirf object literal par lagta hai. Variable se assign karne par nahi — yahi wo behaviour hai jo confuse karta hai.
Structural typing ka matlab hai ki UserId aur PostId (dono string) ek hi hain — asli id mix-up bugs isse aate hain.
Interview mein "TypeScript structural hai, nominal nahi" bata dena — aur ek nuksaan bhi. Wo jawab alag dikhta hai.

lessons.name: keyof & typeof Type Operators
lessons.desc: keyof T yields a union of known public property names of T. typeof gives you the type of a value at the type level — essential for extracting types from values.
lessons.q: What does keyof T produce? How does typeof value differ from a type annotation? Show three real uses of combining keyof and typeof.
lessons.qsub: What is keyof typeof in TypeScript — specifically for extracting keys from a const object? Why is keyof any always string | number | symbol?
terms: Type ki saari keys ka union nikalta hai.
Ek value ka type nikalta hai (type ki duniya mein).
lessons.what:
Do chhote operators jo milkar TypeScript ka sabse zyada use hone wala pattern banate hain.

keyof T = T ki saari keys ka union. typeof x = value x ka type. Dono mila kar: "is object ki keys ka type de do".
lessons.why: Iske bina keys ko haath se likhna padta — aur jis din object mein nayi key jodo, type purana reh jaata aur galti pakdi hi nahi jaati. keyof typeof se type hamesha object ke saath sync rehta hai.
where: K extends keyof T se exact return type.
pros: Type object ke saath hamesha sync rehta hai.
Keys manually likhne ki zarurat khatam.
Generic functions ka return type exact ho jaata hai.
cons: typeof ke do matlab (JS wala aur TS wala) confuse karte hain.
keyof optional aur readonly keys bhi le aata hai.
Nested objects par lambi chain likhni padti hai.
gotchas: typeof type ki jagah likha (annotation mein) TS wala hai; value ki jagah likha JS wala. Ek hi shabd, do duniyaen.
keyof typeof OBJ — ye pattern yaad kar lo. Roz kaam aata hai.
keyof tabhi kaam ka hai jab object as const ho ya uska type saaf ho — warna widened keys milti hain.

lessons.name: Indexed Access Types (T[K])
lessons.desc: T[K] accesses the type at key K within T. Supports nested access, union keys, and extends keyof constraints. Enables type-safe property lookups.
lessons.q: How do you write an indexed access type in TypeScript? Show three examples: simple property, nested property, and union key access.
lessons.qsub: What happens when K is not a valid key of T? How do you constrain K at the type level? What is the difference between T[string] and T[keyof T]?
terms: T[K] — type ke andar se ek field ka type nikalna.
Array type ke andar ka element type.
lessons.what:
Jaise value se user.name nikalte ho, waise hi type se User["name"] nikal sakte ho.

Aur array ke liye T[number] — "is array ke andar kya hai".
lessons.why: Type ko dobara likhna sabse aam bug ki jagah hai — original badla, copy purani reh gayi. Indexed access se aap type ko nikalte ho, likhte nahi. Jo bhi badlega, apne aap sath chalega.
where: Andar ka shape nikalo, dobara mat likho.
pros: Type duplication poori tarah khatam.
Original badla to nikala hua type apne aap badal jaata hai.
Config arrays se types nikalna ek line ka kaam.
cons: Deep chains padhne mein bhaari ho jaati hain.
Error messages tab confusing hote hain.
Optional fields ka | undefined saath aata hai.
gotchas: Dot notation kaam nahi karta — User.address nahi, User["address"].
T[number] array element ke liye hai. Tuple par ye saare elements ka union deta hai.
Nested type dobara likhne ki jagah hamesha nikalo — wahi ek aadat bahut bugs bachati hai.

lessons.name: User-Defined Type Guards
lessons.desc: Functions with return type parameterName is Type act as type predicates. They tell TypeScript to narrow a type if the function returns true.
lessons.q: What is a user-defined type guard? Implement isFish(pet: Fish | Bird): pet is Fish. What exactly does the is keyword do at the type level?
lessons.qsub: Can you use arrow functions as type guards? What happens with type guards on arrays — how do you filter an Array<string | number> to get Array<number>?
terms: Aisa function jo boolean lautaye aur TypeScript ko type bhi bata de.
x is Dog — return type ki jagah likha jaane wala khaas syntax.
lessons.what: Normal function boolean lautata hai — TypeScript ko usse kuch pata nahi chalta. Type guard mein aap boolean ki jagah x is Dog likhte ho, aur ab TS if ke andar type narrow kar deta hai.
lessons.why: Built-in narrowing (typeof, instanceof) sirf simple cases sambhalta hai. Apne shapes ke liye — API response, discriminated union, unknown data — apna guard likhna padta hai. Aur ye as se kahin behtar hai, kyunki as check karta hi nahi, sirf compiler ko chup karata hai.
where: Bahar se aaye data ko safely type dena.
filter((x): x is T => ...) se null hatana.
pros: Runtime check aur compile-time type ek saath.
as ki zarurat khatam.
filter ke saath null hatana type-safe ho jaata hai.
cons: TypeScript aapke guard ka logic check nahi karta — galat guard chup-chaap jhooth bolega.
Deep objects ke liye guard likhna lamba ho jaata hai.
Har type ke liye alag guard maintain karna padta hai.
gotchas: TS aapke guard par bharosa kar leta hai. function isDog(a): a is Dog { return true } compile ho jaayega — jhooth bolna aapki zimmedari hai.
Bade shapes ke liye haath se guard mat likho — Zod jaisi library schema se guard bana deti hai.
filter((x): x is string => ...) — ye annotation likhna zaroori hai, warna type narrow nahi hoga.

lessons.name: Assertion Functions
lessons.desc: Functions that throw if a condition fails, telling the compiler to narrow types (asserts x is T). Added in TypeScript 3.7. Cleaner than if !throw patterns.
lessons.q: What is an assertion function? Write assertIsDefined<T>(val: T | undefined): asserts val is T. How does it differ from a type guard?
lessons.qsub: What are the two forms of assertion return types: asserts condition and asserts value is Type? When would you use each?
terms: Aisa function jo galat hone par throw kare — aur uske baad TS type maan le.
asserts x is T — return type ki jagah likha jaane wala syntax.
lessons.what: Type guard true/false deta hai aur aap if likhte ho. Assertion function galat hone par throw kar deta hai — aur us line ke baad TypeScript maan leta hai ki type sahi hai. Koi if nahi.
lessons.why: Jab galat hona bug hai (recoverable nahi), to if/else likhna shor hai. Assertion se code seedha neeche chalta rehta hai — jaise node:assert, par type safety ke saath.
where: Env variables, config — galat ho to app chalna hi nahi chahiye.
! ki jagah — crash par saaf message milta hai.
"Yahan tak pahunche hain to ye pakka hai" wale checks.
pros: if ki nesting khatam — code seedha padhta hai.
! se behtar — asli check hota hai aur message milta hai.
Ek hi jagah likho, poore file mein narrow rehta hai.
cons: Return type likhna zaroori hai — arrow function ke saath kaam nahi karta.
Variable ka type explicit hona chahiye.
Throw karta hai — recoverable cases ke liye galat.
gotchas: Arrow function se assertion nahi likh sakte — function declaration hi chahiye. Ye TS ki asli limitation hai.
Assertion sirf tab use karo jab galat hona bug ho. Normal cases ke liye type guard + if.
assertDefined jaisa ek generic helper likh lo — ! ki zarurat lagbhag khatam ho jaayegi.

lessons.name: Generics — Constraints & Defaults
lessons.desc: Type parameters that make code reusable across types. Constraints (extends) restrict what T can be. Defaults provide fallback types.
lessons.q: Explain generics deeply. What is a generic constraint? What is a generic default? When does TypeScript fail to infer a generic and you must annotate?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between T extends object and T extends {} and T extends Record<string,unknown>? Which is strictest?
terms: Type ko khaali jagah chhod dena, aur use karte waqt bharna.
lessons.what:
Ek function jo kisi bhi type ke saath chale, par type khoye bina.

any se bhi har type chal jaata hai — par wahan type kho jaata hai. Generic se identity("hi") aapko string wapas deta hai, any nahi.
lessons.why: Generic ka asli kaam input aur output ko jodna hai. function first<T>(arr: T[]): T keh raha hai: "jo bhi andar aayega, wahi bahar jaayega." Wo rishta any se poori tarah toot jaata hai.

visual.cap: any type ko kaat deta hai; generic use aage le jaata hai. Constraint (extends) wo cheez hai jo generic ko use karne layak banati hai.

pros: Ek function, har type — aur type kabhi khota nahi.
Constraint se autocomplete andar bhi chalta hai.
Input aur output ka rishta compiler ko dikh jaata hai.
cons: Zyada type parameters padhne mein bhaari.
Error messages generic code mein lambe hote hain.
Ek hi type ke liye generic banana bekaar hai.
gotchas: Constraint lagana bhoolna sabse aam galti — phir T ke andar kuch use nahi kar paoge aur mann karega any laga do.

Do se zyada type parameters ho jaayein to poore naam do (TItem, TKey) — T, U, V 6 mahine baad kuch nahi batate.

lessons.name: Conditional Types
lessons.desc: T extends U ? X : Y — evaluated at the type level. Distributes over union members by default. Enables type-level computation.
lessons.q: How do conditional types work? What is distributive behaviour over unions and when does it produce surprising results?
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent distribution? What is [T] extends [U] vs T extends U — why does wrapping in a tuple stop distribution?
terms: Type ki duniya ka if-else — A extends B ? X : Y.
Inheritance nahi — "kya ye us type mein fit hota hai?"
lessons.what:
Type level par if. Padho aise: "agar A, B mein fit hota hai to X, warna Y".

Yahan extends ka matlab inheritance nahi hai — matlab hai "assignable hai kya".
lessons.why: Iske bina aapko har case ke liye alag type likhna padta. Conditional types se ek type apne input ke hisaab se badal sakta hai — aur Exclude, ReturnType, Awaited jaise saare utility types isi par khade hain.
where: Success aur error ke alag shapes ek type se.
Input ke hisaab se return type badalna.
pros: Ek type kai cases sambhal leta hai.
Saare built-in utility types isi se bane hain — samajh aane par wo khul jaate hain.
infer ke saath type ke andar se cheezein nikal sakte ho.
cons: Nested conditionals bahut jaldi padhne layak nahi rehte.
Union par distribute hona chaunkata hai.
Error messages lagbhag samajh se bahar ho jaate hain.
gotchas: Yahan extends ka matlab "assignable hai kya" hai, inheritance nahi. Ye samajhna aadha kaam hai.
Naked type parameter union par distribute ho jaata hai — Wrap<A|B> se A[]|B[] milta hai. Rokne ke liye [T] extends [X].
Teen se zyada nested conditions ho jaayein to ruk kar sochо — aksar ek simple overload behtar hota hai.

lessons.name: Mapped Types
lessons.desc: Transform every property of an existing type: { [K in keyof T]: ... }. Used to build Partial, Readonly, Pick, and custom transformations.
lessons.q: What are mapped types? Build Partial<T>, Readonly<T>, and Nullable<T> from scratch using only mapped types and no built-in utilities.
lessons.qsub: What are mapping modifiers (+ and -)? How do you use -? and -readonly to build Required<T> and Mutable<T>?
terms: Ek type ki saari keys par ghoom kar naya type banana.
readonly aur ? — inhe +/- se jod-hata sakte ho.
lessons.what:
Jaise array.map() har item par ghoomta hai, waise mapped type har key par ghoomta hai aur naya type banata hai.

Partial, Required, Readonly, Record — ye chaaron mapped types hain, aur chaaron 2-3 line ke hain.
lessons.why: Iske bina "User ka wahi shape par sab optional" likhne ke liye poora interface dobara likhna padta — aur jis din original badla, copy purani reh gayi. Mapped type se copy hamesha sync rehti hai.
where: Har field ke saath error aur touched.
Create/Update ke liye alag shapes ek base se.
pros: Type duplication khatam — original badla to sab badal gaya.
-? aur -readonly se modifiers hata sakte ho.
Built-in utilities ka andar ka kaam khul jaata hai.
cons: Nested objects par apne aap deep nahi hota.
Error messages expand hokar bahut lambe ho jaate hain.
Syntax shuru mein ajeeb lagta hai.
gotchas: Partial shallow hai — nested object optional nahi hota. DeepPartial khud recursive likhna padta hai.
-? aur -readonly — minus se modifier hataya jaata hai. Ye bahut kam log jaante hain.
[K in keyof T] optional/readonly modifiers apne aap saath le aata hai, jab tak aap unhe hataao nahi.

lessons.name: Template Literal Types
lessons.desc: Combine string literal types using template syntax: `${A}${B}`. Enables type-safe event names, CSS properties, and path strings.
lessons.q: What are template literal types? Show 3 real-world use cases where they catch bugs at compile time that would otherwise be silent runtime errors.
lessons.qsub: How do you combine template literal types with mapped types to create a type-safe EventEmitter where each event name has a typed payload?
terms: String types ko jod kar naya string type banana.
lessons.what:
Jaise value level par backtick string mein ${name} likh kar jodte ho, waise hi type level par string types jod sakte ho.

Union ke saath mila do to ye saare combinations bana deta hai — automatically.
lessons.why: Isse aap API routes, event names aur CSS properties ko type-safe bana sakte ho — bina haath se saare naam likhe. Typo likhte waqt pakda jaata hai, chalte waqt nahi.
pros: Combinations apne aap ban jaate hain.
String format compile time par check hota hai.
Key remapping ke saath bahut powerful.
cons: Bade unions par combination explosion — compiler slow ya fail.
Error messages mein poora union print ho jaata hai.
Debug karna mushkil.
gotchas: Combination explosion asli problem hai — chaar 5-member unions = 625 types. Editor slow ho jaayega.
${string} ka matlab "koi bhi string" — usse format enforce hota hai par values nahi.
Interview mein iska ek asli use bata dena (design system classes ya event names) — sirf syntax jaanna kaafi nahi.

lessons.name: The infer Keyword
lessons.desc: Extract a type from within a conditional type. Used to pull out return types, promise values, array element types, and function parameters.
lessons.q: What does infer do inside a conditional type? Implement ReturnType<T>, Awaited<T>, and UnpackArray<T> using infer from scratch.
lessons.qsub: How does infer interact with covariant vs contravariant positions? Why does inferring from a function parameter position behave differently than inferring from a return type?
terms: Conditional type ke andar "yahan jo bhi hai use pakad lo aur naam de do".
lessons.what:
infer ka ek hi kaam hai: kisi type ke andar se ek hissa nikal lena.

Padho aise: "agar T Promise<kuch> jaisa dikhta hai, to us kuch ko U naam do aur wahi lauta do."
lessons.why: ReturnType, Parameters, Awaited — ye sab infer se bane hain. Aur aapke apne code mein iska sabse aam use hai: function ka return type nikal kar use type ki tarah use karna, taaki dono kabhi alag na hon.
where: User ke diye type ke andar se hissa nikalna.
pros: Type ke andar se hissa nikalna — dobara likhne ki zarurat nahi.
Sab built-in utilities khul kar samajh aa jaate hain.
ReturnType<typeof fn> se type aur code kabhi alag nahi hote.
cons: Sirf conditional type ke andar chalta hai.
Padhna mushkil — team mein sab nahi samajhte.
Kai infer ek saath ho to debug karna dard hai.
gotchas: infer sirf extends ? : ke andar likha ja sakta hai — kahin aur syntax error hai.
Apne roz ke code mein aapko shayad kabhi likhna na pade — par ReturnType<typeof fn> roz kaam aayega.
Interview mein "utility types kaise bante hain" poocha jaaye to infer hi jawab hai.

lessons.name: Recursive & Deep Types
lessons.desc: Types that reference themselves — for trees, nested JSON, deeply nested objects. TypeScript supports recursive types with some depth limits.
lessons.q: How do you define a recursive type in TypeScript? Implement DeepPartial<T> and DeepReadonly<T>.
lessons.qsub: What are the TypeScript limits on recursive type instantiation depth? How do you work around them using the "lazy evaluation" tuple trick?
terms: Aisa type jo apne andar khud ko use kare.
TypeScript ~50 level tak hi jaata hai, phir haar maan leta hai.
lessons.what:
Type khud ko reference kar sakta hai — jaise recursive function. JSON, tree, nested config — sab isi se model hote hain.

Aur mapped types ke saath mila kar aap DeepPartial jaise utilities bana sakte ho.
lessons.why: Built-in Partial, Readonly sab shallow hain — sirf upar ka level. Nested config ya API response ke liye deep chahiye hota hai, aur wo recursion se hi banta hai.
where: Bahar se aaye data ka type.
pros: Nested structures theek se model ho jaate hain.
Built-in shallow utilities ka deep version bana sakte ho.
Kisi bhi depth par kaam karta hai.
cons: ~50 level ki hard limit hai.
Compiler slow ho jaata hai bade recursive types par.
Error messages poora expand hokar aate hain.
gotchas: DeepPartial likhte waqt Date, Array aur Function ko alag handle karo — warna Date ke andar ke fields bhi optional ban jaate hain.
"Excessively deep" error ka matlab aksar infinite recursion hota hai, sach mein 50-level data nahi.
Har jagah deep utilities mat lagao — wo compiler ko dhima karte hain aur aksar shallow hi kaafi hota hai.

lessons.name: Variadic Tuple Types
lessons.desc: Tuple types can spread other tuples using ...T syntax — enables typed rest parameters, Concat, Zip, and function argument manipulation.
lessons.q: What are variadic tuple types? How do they enable building typed Concat<A,B> or typed function composition with exact argument types?
lessons.qsub: How does TypeScript use variadic tuples internally to type Promise.all correctly — preserving the type of each resolved value?
terms: Fixed length aur fixed order wala array — [string, number].
Tuple ke andar ...T — "baaki jo bhi ho".
lessons.what:
Tuple types ke andar spread (...) use karna. Isse aap "pehla argument ye, baaki jo bhi ho" jaise types likh sakte ho.

Imaandari se: ye roz kaam nahi aata. Ye tab chahiye jab aap bind, curry ya pipe jaise function transform karne wale utilities likh rahe ho.
lessons.why: Iske bina "pehla argument hata do, baaki return kar do" jaisa type likha hi nahi ja sakta tha — aur bind/partial ke types galat rehte the.
where: Kisi function ko lapetna aur uske arguments preserve karna.
Roz ke app code mein lagbhag kabhi nahi.
pros: Function-transforming utilities ke types sahi ban jaate hain.
Arguments ka rishta poora preserve rehta hai.
Tuple labels padhne mein madad karte hain.
cons: App code mein lagbhag kabhi zarurat nahi.
Padhna aur debug karna mushkil.
Error messages bahut bhaari.
gotchas: Ye library-level feature hai. Roz ke code mein zarurat pade to shayad design over-complicated hai.
Tuple labels ([x: number]) sirf documentation hain — runtime par kuch nahi.
Interview mein iska naam jaanna kaafi hai; is par gehrai poochhi jaaye to wo library-author wala role hai.

lessons.name: Distributive Conditional Types
lessons.desc: When a conditional type acts on a generic type T that is a union, it distributes over each member. This enables type-level operations like Exclude, Extract, and custom filters.
lessons.q: What is distribution in conditional types? Why does T extends U ? X : Y distribute over unions of T? Show how Exclude<T,U> leverages this.
lessons.qsub: How do you PREVENT distribution (the tuple trick [T] extends [U])? When is distribution harmful and you need to suppress it? How does never behave in distribution?
terms: Conditional type ka union ke har member par alag-alag chalna.
T extends X — jahan T akela likha ho, bina bracket ke.
lessons.what:
Jab conditional type ka input ek union ho aur T akela likha ho, TypeScript us type ko union ke har member par alag chalata hai aur nateeje ko dobara union bana deta hai.

Ye aksar chahiye hota hai — aur kabhi-kabhi bilkul nahi.
lessons.why: Exclude aur Extract isi behaviour par khade hain. Aur jab ye nahi chahiye, tab bracket lagana ([T] extends [X]) hi wo trick hai jo bahut log nahi jaante — aur jiski wajah se unke types ajeeb behave karte hain.

visual.cap: Naked T union par bat jaata hai; bracket lagane par poora union ek saath check hota hai. Exclude/Extract pehle wale par khade hain.

where: Har member ko alag treat karna.
Jab conditional type union par ajeeb behave kare.
pros: Union ka har member apne aap handle ho jaata hai.
Exclude/Extract isi se possible hain.
Bracket se poora control mil jaata hai.
cons: Chup-chaap hota hai — pata hi nahi chalta.
never aur boolean par behaviour chaunkata hai.
Debug karna mushkil.
gotchas: Wrap<never> = never, kyunki never khaali union hai aur distribute karne ko kuch hai hi nahi.
boolean asal mein true | false hai — isliye wo bhi distribute hota hai.
Bracket wala trick ([T] extends [X]) yaad rakho — jab conditional type ajeeb behave kare, 90% baar yahi jawab hai.

lessons.name: Key Remapping via as Clauses
lessons.desc: Mapped types support key remapping with as: { [K in keyof T as NewKey]: T[K] }. Enables prefixing, suffixing, filtering, and transforming object keys at the type level.
lessons.q: What is key remapping in TypeScript mapped types? Show how to: prefix all keys with "_", filter out functions from an object type, and make all keys optional.
lessons.qsub: How do you combine key remapping with template literal types to create a type-safe getter/setter pair for every property? What is the Capitalize<StringType> intrinsic used for?
terms: Mapped type ke andar as se keys ke naam badalna.
Key ko never bana do to wo poori tarah hat jaati hai.
lessons.what: Mapped type mein as lagakar aap key ka naam badal sakte ho — ya use never banakar hata sakte ho.
lessons.why: Isse do kaam hote hain jo pehle namumkin the: naam ke pattern se keys banana (name → getName), aur type ke hisaab se keys filter karna (sirf string wali keys chaahiye).
where: Field naam se method naam banana.
pros: Keys ke naam pattern se ban jaate hain.
never se filter karna bahut saaf tarika hai.
Template literal types ke saath bahut powerful.
cons: Padhne mein bhaari.
K & string jaisa jugaad yaad rakhna padta hai.
Error messages samajhna mushkil.
gotchas: as never se key gayab ho jaati hai — filter karne ka yahi tarika hai.
Capitalize<K> nahi chalega, Capitalize<K & string> chahiye — kyunki keys mein symbol bhi ho sakta hai.
Ye TS 4.1+ ka feature hai. Purane version mein ye syntax error hai.

lessons.name: Intrinsic String Manipulation Types
lessons.desc: TypeScript 4.1+ provides Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, Uncapitalize as intrinsic types — handled by the compiler, not expressible in userland. Used in template literal type transformations.
lessons.q: What are intrinsic string types in TypeScript? Show how Capitalize, Uncapitalize, Uppercase, and Lowercase work. Why are they "intrinsic" and not implementable by users?
lessons.qsub: How do you use Capitalize with template literals to convert snake_case to camelCase at the type level? What are the performance implications of deeply nested string type transformations?
terms: Compiler ke andar bana hua — TypeScript mein likha hi nahi ja sakta.
lessons.what:
Chaar built-in string types: Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, Uncapitalize.

Ye intrinsic hain — matlab compiler ke andar C++ mein likhe hain, TypeScript mein nahi. Isliye aap inhe khud nahi bana sakte.
lessons.why: String manipulation type level par karna aur koi tarika nahi tha. In chaaron se template literal types sach mein kaam ke ban jaate hain — onClick, getName jaise patterns inhi se bante hain.
pros: Type level par string manipulation mumkin ho jaata hai.
Compiler ke andar bane hain — bahut tez.
Template literal types ke saath poora pattern bana dete hain.
cons: Sirf chaar hain — Trim, Split, Replace nahi.
Khud nahi bana sakte.
Baaki string ops recursive types se banane padte hain, jo slow hain.
gotchas: Ye chaaron intrinsic hain — TypeScript mein likhe hi nahi ja sakte. Interview mein ye bata dena ek achha detail hai.
Trim ya Split chahiye to recursive template literal types khud likhne padenge — aur wo compiler ko dhima karte hain.
Union par ye distribute hote hain — Uppercase<"a"|"b"> se "A"|"B" milta hai.

lessons.name: Abstract Classes — abstract methods, constructor access, vs interfaces
lessons.desc: Abstract classes can't be instantiated directly. Abstract methods have no body — subclasses must implement them. Unlike interfaces, abstract classes can have constructors, state, and concrete methods. Use when you need shared implementation across related classes.
lessons.q: What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface in TypeScript? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: Can an abstract class have a constructor? How do you implement abstract methods in a subclass?
terms: Adhoori class — usse seedha object nahi ban sakta.
Sirf naam, koi body nahi — bachche ko likhna padega.
lessons.what:
Ek class jo adhoori hai. Usme kuch methods poori hoti hain (sabke liye same) aur kuch abstract — jo har bachche ko khud likhni padti hain.

new AbstractClass() nahi chalta — pehle use poora karna padta hai.
lessons.why:
Interface se farak sirf ek hai: abstract class code de sakti hai, interface nahi. Aur ek class sirf ek abstract class extend kar sakti hai, par kai interfaces implement kar sakti hai.

Isliye niyam: saanjha code hai → abstract class. Sirf waada hai → interface.
where: Kram fixed, kuch kadam bachche bharte hain.
Jahan users ko extend karna ho.
pros: Saanjha code ek jagah, aur compiler baaki likhwa leta hai.
Bachche kuch bhoolein to compile time par pakda jaata hai.
Type ki tarah bhi use ho sakti hai.
cons: Ek hi baap — do jagah se code chahiye to kaam nahi karta.
Deep hierarchy jaldi bhaari ho jaati hai.
JS mein aksar composition behtar hota hai.
gotchas: abstract chalte waqt gayab ho jaata hai — wo sirf compiler ka lebal hai. Compile ke baad wo normal class hai.
Abstract class ko new (...) => T type mein pass nahi kar sakte — factory pattern mein ye trap karta hai.
Faisla ek line mein: saanjha code → abstract class; sirf waada → interface; kai roop → interface.

lessons.name: Variance Annotations — in, out, invariant on type parameters
lessons.desc: TypeScript 4.7+ supports variance annotations: out T (covariant), in T (contravariant), in out T (invariant). Controls how type parameter subtyping works. Methods are contravariant in parameters, covariant in return types by default with strictFunctionTypes.
lessons.q: What are variance annotations in TypeScript? What does `in` and `out` mean on a type parameter?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between covariance and contravariance? Give a practical example with function types.
terms: Type parameter sirf bahar aata hai (return position).
Type parameter sirf andar jaata hai (parameter position).
Dono jagah — to na chauda kar sakte ho na patla.
lessons.what:
TypeScript khud pata laga leta hai ki generic type parameter kaise behave karta hai. in/out se aap wo likh kar bata sakte ho.

Imaandari se: ye 99% code mein zarurat nahi padta. Do wajah hain iske hone ki — bade codebase mein compiler tez ho jaata hai, aur aapka iraada document ho jaata hai.
lessons.why: Bina annotation ke TypeScript har generic type ki variance khud calculate karta hai — jo bade projects mein slow hai. Annotation likh dene se wo calculation skip ho jaati hai.
pros: Bade projects mein type-checking tez ho jaati hai.
Aapka iraada types mein likha hua hota hai.
Galat use compile time par pakda jaata hai.
cons: App code mein lagbhag bekaar.
Galat annotation ulta error banata hai.
TS 4.7+ chahiye.
gotchas: Ye performance aur documentation ka feature hai, correctness ka nahi — TypeScript ye khud calculate kar hi leta hai.
Yaad rakhne ka tarika: out = bahar aata hai (return), in = andar jaata hai (parameter).
Interview mein iska naam pata hona kaafi hai. Gehrai poochhi jaaye to wo compiler-team level ka sawaal hai.

lessons.name: Partial, Required, Readonly
lessons.desc: Partial makes all props optional. Required makes all required. Readonly prevents reassignment. None are deep — they only affect the top level.
lessons.q: Implement Partial<T>, Required<T>, Readonly<T> from scratch using mapped types. What are their limitations (shallow only)?
lessons.qsub: Does Readonly<T> prevent mutating nested object properties? Why not? Implement DeepReadonly<T> using recursive conditional types.
terms: Saare fields badalne se rok do.
lessons.what:
Teen mapped types jo ek hi type ke alag-alag roop bana dete hain — bina poora interface dobara likhe.

Teeno ka andar ka code 2-2 line ka hai, aur teeno shallow hain.
lessons.why: Ek hi cheez ke aksar teen shapes chahiye hote hain: banate waqt (id nahi hoti), update karte waqt (sab optional), aur padhte waqt (sab zaroori). Inhe haath se likhoge to jis din base badla, teeno purane reh jaayenge.
where: Partial<T> — user sirf kuch fields bhejta hai.
pros: Ek base se saare variants — duplication zero.
Base badla to sab apne aap badal gaye.
Padhne mein saaf — iraada dikh jaata hai.
cons: Teeno shallow hain — nested par kaam nahi.
Partial ka zyada use zaroori fields chhupa deta hai.
Readonly sirf compile time — chalte waqt object badla ja sakta hai.
gotchas: Sab shallow hain. Nested chahiye to DeepPartial khud recursive likhna padega.
Readonly compile-time hai. Chalte waqt bhi rokna hai to Object.freeze chahiye.
Har jagah Partial mat lagao — phir compiler ko pata hi nahi rehta ki kya zaroori hai.

lessons.name: Pick, Omit, Extract, Exclude
lessons.desc: Pick/Omit work on object keys. Extract/Exclude work on union members. They are often confused because the names are symmetrical.
lessons.q: What is the difference between Omit<T,K> and Exclude<T,K>? What is the difference between Pick<T,K> and Extract<T,K>? Give concrete examples.
lessons.qsub: Implement Pick<T,K> and Omit<T,K> from scratch. Why does Omit have a known quirk with discriminated unions — and what is the fix?
terms: Union par kaam karte hain, object par nahi.
lessons.what:
Chaar utilities, do jodiyan — aur ye jodiyan alag cheezon par kaam karti hain, jo sabse aam confusion hai.

Pick/Omit → object ki keys par.
Extract/Exclude → union ke members par.
lessons.why: Aksar aapko poore type ka ek hissa chahiye hota hai — ek component ko sirf teen fields, ek API ko sirf public fields. Naya interface likhne se do jagah maintain karni padti hain; Pick/Omit se ek.
where: Base component ke props ka hissa lena.
Ek state hata kar baaki par kaam.
pros: Ek base se hissa nikalna — duplication khatam.
Base badla to hissa bhi badal gaya.
Omit se sensitive fields nikalna ek line ka kaam.
cons: Omit galat key naam par error nahi deta.
Union aur object wali jodiyan aapas mein confuse hoti hain.
Chain lambi ho to error messages bhaari.
gotchas: Omit key ka naam validate nahi karta — Omit<User, "passwrod"> chup-chaap chal jaata hai aur field rah jaati hai. StrictOmit helper likh lo.
Pick/Omit objects par, Extract/Exclude unions par — ye do jodiyan mat gadbadao.
Omit discriminated union ko tod deta hai — wo union ko ek object bana deta hai. Union par Exclude use karo.

lessons.name: Record<K,V>
lessons.desc: Creates an object type with keys of type K and values of type V. Stronger than { [key: string]: V } because it enforces all union keys are present.
lessons.q: When is Record<K,V> better than { [key: string]: V }? How does Record with a union key enforce exhaustive key handling?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between Record<string,V> and { [key: string]: V } in terms of excess property checking and index signature behaviour?
terms: Aisa object jiski saari keys K type ki hon aur values V type ki.
lessons.what:
Record<K, V> = "in keys wala object, jinki values V type ki hon".

Andar se ye ek line ka mapped type hai: { [P in K]: V }.
lessons.why: Iska sabse bada faayda ye hai ki agar K ek union hai, to TypeScript har member ko zaroori bana deta hai. Naya status add karo aur uska handler likhna bhool jao — compile error. Plain object se ye kabhi nahi hota.
pros: Union key ke saath har case zaroori ho jaata hai.
Naya member add karne par compiler yaad dilaata hai.
Padhne mein { [k: string]: T } se saaf.
cons: Record<string, T> jhoothi suraksha deta hai — har key "hai" lagti hai.
Optional keys ke liye Partial lapetna padta hai.
Bade unions par error messages lambe.
gotchas: Record<string, T> par har lookup "mil gaya" maana jaata hai — noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true on karo ya Partial lapetо.
Union key ke saath ye exhaustiveness check deta hai — yahi iska sabse bada faayda hai.
Record<K, V> aur { [P in K]: V } bilkul ek hi cheez hain.

lessons.name: ReturnType, Parameters, ConstructorParameters
lessons.desc: Extract types from function signatures without repeating them — essential for wrappers, decorators, and middleware.
lessons.q: What does ReturnType<T> do internally (hint: infer)? Show 3 real use cases for Parameters<T> and ReturnType<T> in production code.
lessons.qsub: How do you extract the type of the second argument of a function using Parameters<T> and tuple indexing? What about optional parameters?
terms: Function ke arguments ka tuple nikalo.
lessons.what:
Function se type nikalne wale utilities. Teeno infer se bane hain.

Aur inka sabse kaam ka pattern ek hi hai: ReturnType<typeof fn>.
lessons.why: Function ka return shape alag se interface likhoge to jis din function badla, interface purana reh jaayega — aur galti pakdi nahi jaayegi. Nikaal lene se dono kabhi alag nahi ho sakte.
where: Redux/Zustand — state ka shape nikal lo.
Factory function se object ka type.
pros: Type aur code kabhi alag nahi ho sakte.
Interface likhne ki zarurat khatam.
Awaited ke saath async bhi sambhal jaata hai.
cons: Overloaded function par sirf aakhri overload milta hai.
Generic function par unknown aa jaata hai.
Type padh kar shape dikhta nahi — function kholna padta hai.
gotchas: typeof lagana zaroori hai — ReturnType<makeUser> galat hai, ReturnType<typeof makeUser> sahi.
Async function par Awaited<ReturnType<...>> chahiye — warna Promise<T> milega.
Overloads par ye sirf aakhri signature dekhta hai — silent galti ki jagah.

lessons.name: Awaited<T> & Async Types
lessons.desc: Recursively unwraps Promise<T> to get T. Handles nested Promises and thenables. Added in TS 4.5 to replace the broken ReturnType<AsyncFn> pattern.
lessons.q: Why was Awaited<T> added in TypeScript 4.5? What was broken about using ReturnType to type async functions before it?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between Promise<T>, PromiseLike<T>, and a thenable? Which should library types accept for maximum compatibility?
terms: Promise ke andar ki value ka type — chahe kitni bhi layers ho.
lessons.what: Awaited<Promise<string>> = string. Aur agar promise ke andar promise ho, to wo bhi khol deta hai — jaise await khud karta hai.
lessons.why: Pehle log T extends Promise<infer U> ? U : T khud likhte the — par wo nested promises aur thenable objects par galat tha. Awaited wo sab sahi karta hai.
where: Async function se response type nikalna.
pros: Nested promises apne aap khul jaate hain.
Plain values par kuch nahi karta — safe hai.
Thenable objects bhi sahi handle karta hai.
cons: Log ReturnType ke saath lagana bhool jaate hain.
Type padhne mein lamba ho jaata hai.
TS 4.5+ chahiye.
gotchas: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fn>> — ye poora pattern yaad rakho, roz kaam aayega.
Khud T extends Promise<infer U> mat likho — wo nested promises par galat hai.
Plain type par lagane se kuch nahi bigadta — safe hai, isliye shak ho to laga do.

lessons.name: Building Custom Utility Types
lessons.desc: Combine generics, conditional types, mapped types, and infer to create domain-specific utility types.
lessons.q: Build these from scratch: DeepPartial<T>, Mutable<T> (reverse of Readonly), FunctionKeys<T> (only keys whose values are functions).
lessons.qsub: Build OverrideProps<Base, Override> that merges two object types where Override wins on conflicts. How is this different from Base & Override?
terms: Apna banaya hua reusable type helper.
lessons.what:
Built-in utilities kaafi nahi padte. Kuch helpers har project mein chahiye hote hain aur TypeScript unhe deta nahi.

Yahan wo paanch hain jo sabse zyada kaam aate hain.
lessons.why: Ek types/utils.ts file bana lo aur ye helpers wahan rakho. Ek baar likho, poore project mein use karo — aur naye logon ko wahi file padh kar project ka type style samajh aa jaata hai.
pros: Ek baar likho, har jagah use karo.
Prettify se editor mein types padhne layak ho jaate hain.
Project ka type style ek file mein document ho jaata hai.
cons: Complex helpers ke error messages bahut bhaari.
Zyada abstraction se naye log confuse hote hain.
Recursive helpers compiler ko dhima karte hain.
gotchas: Prettify<T> (& {} wala trick) sabse under-rated helper hai — wo type ko hover par flat karke dikhata hai.
DeepPartial mein Date aur Array ko alag handle karna zaroori hai, warna Date ke fields optional ban jaate hain.
5-6 se zyada custom utilities ho jaayein to ruk kar sochо — shayad types over-engineered hain.

lessons.name: NonNullable & Null Handling Utilities
lessons.desc: NonNullable<T> removes null and undefined from T. Useful after filter(Boolean) or in combination with Partial. Not deep — only removes top-level nullability.
lessons.q: What does NonNullable<T> do? Implement it from scratch. Why does Array<T>.filter(Boolean) not automatically narrow the type to NonNullable<T>?
lessons.qsub: How do you write a type-safe filter(Boolean) wrapper that returns NonNullable<T>[]? What is the difference between NonNullable and Exclude<T, null | undefined>?
lessons.what:
Ek line ka utility: NonNullable<string | null> = string.

Andar se: T extends null | undefined ? never : T.
lessons.why: Aksar aapko pata hota hai ki is point par value null nahi ho sakti — filter ke baad, guard ke baad. NonNullable se ye type mein likh sakte ho, bina ! lagaye.
pros: ! ki zarurat khatam.
filter ke saath type sahi ho jaata hai.
Ek line ka helper — samajhna aasan.
cons: filter(Boolean) ke saath apne aap kaam nahi karta.
Runtime par kuch nahi karta — sirf type level.
Zyada use ho to shayad type shuru se hi galat hai.
gotchas: items.filter(Boolean) type narrow nahi karta — TS ko Boolean se kuch pata nahi chalta. Apna isDefined guard likho.
filter(Boolean) 0 aur "" bhi hata deta hai — x != null se sirf null/undefined hatte hain.
Ek global isDefined helper bana lo — wo poore project mein sabse zyada use hone wala type helper banega.

lessons.name: NoInfer<T> & Inference Control
lessons.desc: NoInfer<T> (TS 5.4+) prevents TypeScript from using that position for generic inference. Forces callers to provide a type explicitly while still constraining it.
lessons.q: What does NoInfer<T> do? Show a use case where it prevents TypeScript from inferring a too-wide type from one parameter versus another.
lessons.qsub: How did developers prevent inference before NoInfer was added to TypeScript (the phantom type parameter hack)? Why was NoInfer added as an intrinsic type?
terms: TypeScript se kaho: "is jagah se type mat pehchano".
lessons.what:
Jab ek generic type do jagah aata hai, TypeScript dono se infer karta hai aur unhe mila deta hai — aur nateeja aksar chauda ho jaata hai.

NoInfer<T> se aap ek jagah ko inference se bahar kar dete ho.
lessons.why: Ye TS 5.4 ka naya utility hai aur ek purani chidh theek karta hai: default value ki wajah se type chauda ho jaana, jisse galat value bhi pass ho jaati thi.
where: Users ko galat value pass karne se rokna.
Kabhi-kabhi — par jab chahiye tab bahut kaam ka.
pros: Purani inference-widening wali chidh khatam.
Library APIs ko sakht bana deta hai.
TS 5.4 se built-in — jugaad ki zarurat nahi.
cons: TS 5.4+ chahiye.
Kam log jaante hain — code review mein sawaal aayenge.
App code mein kam hi zarurat padti hai.
gotchas: Sochne ka tarika: "type kis argument se aana chahiye?" — baaki sab par NoInfer laga do.
Argument ka order maayne rakhta hai — list pehle, default baad mein.
TS 5.4 se pehle wala jugaad ([T][T extends any ? 0 : never]) purane codebase mein mil sakta hai.

lessons.name: ThisType<T> & ThisParameterType
lessons.desc: ThisType<T> defines the this context inside an object literal (used in Vue options API, Svelte, and chain builders). ThisParameterType and OmitThisParameter extract/remove the this parameter from a function.
lessons.q: What does ThisType<T> do? How is it used in framework types like Vue's Options API? What happens without it?
lessons.qsub: What are ThisParameterType<T> and OmitThisParameter<T>? How do you strip the this parameter from a method type to get its callable signature?
terms: Object literal ke andar this ka type set karo.
Function ke this parameter ka type nikalo.
lessons.what:
Do bahut kam use hone wale utilities jo this ke saath kaam karte hain.

Imaandari se: ThisType ki zarurat aaj lagbhag nahi padti — wo Vue 2 jaise this-based APIs ke liye tha. Par interview mein naam aa jaata hai.
lessons.why: Vue 2 mein aap methods: { greet() { this.name } } likhte the — this ko data tak pahunchna padta tha. ThisType se library author wo type-safe bana sakta tha.
where: this: HTMLElement parameter — ye kaam ka hai.
pros: this-based APIs type-safe ban jaate hain.
this parameter DOM handlers mein sach mein kaam ka hai.
Compile ke baad gayab — koi runtime cost nahi.
cons: ThisType aaj lagbhag bekaar hai.
Modern React/Vue 3 mein this use hi nahi hota.
Padhne mein bhaari.
gotchas: this parameter nakli hai — wo compile ke baad gayab ho jaata hai aur pehla asli argument doosra hi rehta hai.
ThisType tabhi kaam karta hai jab noImplicitThis on ho.
Naye code mein this se bacho — arrow functions aur closures se kaam chal jaata hai.

lessons.name: Intrinsic String Utilities
lessons.desc: Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, Uncapitalize are built-in intrinsic types. Frequently used with template literal types for key transformation and naming convention enforcement.
lessons.q: List all 4 intrinsic string utilities. Show how to build a type that converts camelCase to kebab-case and back using these utilities.
lessons.qsub: What are the limitations of intrinsic string types? Can they handle complex Unicode characters (accents, emojis)? How does TypeScript handle case transformation for non-English characters?
terms: Compiler ke andar bana hua — TypeScript mein likha hi nahi ja sakta.
lessons.what:
Chaar string utilities: Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, Uncapitalize.

In par poori lesson "Intrinsic String Manipulation Types" mein hai — yahan bas ye yaad rakho ki ye utility types ke parivaar ka hissa hain aur baaki utilities se alag hain: baaki TypeScript mein likhe hain, ye compiler ke andar.
lessons.why: Farak maayne rakhta hai kyunki iska matlab hai ki aap Trim, Split, Replace jaise aur helpers khud nahi bana sakte — unke liye recursive template literal types likhne padte hain, jo compiler ko dhima karte hain.
where: "Kaunse utility types compiler ke andar hain?" — achha detail.
pros: Compiler ke andar bane hain — bahut tez.
Template literal types ko kaam ka bana dete hain.
Union par apne aap distribute hote hain.
cons: Sirf chaar hain.
Khud nahi bana sakte.
Baaki string ops recursive types se, jo slow hain.
gotchas: Ye chaar intrinsic hain — baaki saare utility types TypeScript mein hi likhe hue hain aur aap unhe khol kar padh sakte ho.
Trim/Split recursive template literals se banते hain — chhoti strings par theek, badi par compiler slow.
Poori detail "Intrinsic String Manipulation Types" lesson mein hai — yahan sirf parivaar ka farak yaad rakho.

lessons.name: tsconfig.json — Key Options
lessons.desc: Controls strict checks, compilation target, module output format, path aliases, and project references. Getting tsconfig wrong causes silent runtime bugs.
lessons.q: Explain these 10 tsconfig options: strict, target, module, moduleResolution, esModuleInterop, paths, baseUrl, isolatedModules, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between moduleResolution: node, bundler, and node16? Which should you use for a modern Next.js app vs a Node.js ESM library?
terms: TypeScript ki settings file — project ki jad.
Doosri config se settings udhaar lena.
lessons.what:
Ek file jo tay karti hai ki TypeScript kitna sakht hoga, kaunsi files dekhega, aur output kaisa banayega.

Ismein 100+ options hain. Sirf 8-10 sach mein maayne rakhte hain — baaki default theek hain.
lessons.why: Zyadatar "TypeScript ne mujhe nahi bachaya" wali shikayat ek galat config se aati hai — strict off tha. Ek line badalne se TypeScript ka aadha faayda wapas aa jaata hai.
where: extends se ek base config sab jagah.
"Ye error kyu nahi aayi?" — pehle config dekho.
pros: strict: true ek line mein 8 flags de deta hai.
skipLibCheck se build bahut tez.
extends se monorepo mein ek jagah settings.
cons: 100+ options — naye logon ke liye daraavna.
paths bundler ko alag se batana padta hai.
Galat target/lib se ajeeb errors aate hain.
gotchas: "strict": true hamesha. Iske bina TypeScript aadha soya rehta hai.
paths sirf type-checking ke liye hai — bundler (Vite/webpack) ko alag se alias batana padta hai, warna chalte waqt module nahi milega.
skipLibCheck: true lagbhag hamesha chahiye — bina uske node_modules ke types check hote hain aur build slow ho jaata hai.

lessons.name: strict Mode — All 8 Flags
lessons.desc: strict enables: strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, strictPropertyInitialization, strictBindCallApply, strictBuiltinIteratorReturn, useUnknownInCatchVariables, noImplicitThis.
lessons.q: What are all the flags that strict enables? Which ones cause the most pain when enabling on a legacy JavaScript codebase?
lessons.qsub: What is strictFunctionTypes and how does it enforce function parameter contravariance? Give a real example of the bug it prevents.
terms: Ek switch jo 8 alag flags on kar deta hai.
Inme se sabse zyada faayda dene wala.
lessons.what:
"strict": true ek shortcut hai — wo 8 alag flags on karta hai. Har ek apni tarah ki galti pakadta hai.

Inme se strictNullChecks akela hi TypeScript ka aadha faayda deta hai.
