where: Pehle din on karo — baad mein karna 10x mushkil.
"strict off kyu hai?" — hamesha poochne layak sawaal.
pros: Ek line mein 8 tarah ki galtiyan pakdi jaane lagti hain.
strictNullChecks akela sabse aam JS crash rok deta hai.
useUnknownInCatchVariables catch block ko safe banata hai.
cons: Purane codebase mein sau errors ek saath.
strictPropertyInitialization classes ke saath chidhata hai.
Log ! aur any se chup kara dete hain.
gotchas: class A { name!: string } ka ! ka matlab "main sambhaal lunga" hai — agar nahi sambhala to chalte waqt undefined.
catch (e) mein e ab unknown hai — e instanceof Error check karna padega. Ye achha badlav hai.
Purane project mein migrate karte waqt: strict on karo aur ek-ek file par // @ts-nocheck lagao, phir ek-ek karke hataao.

lessons.name: Declaration Files (.d.ts)
lessons.desc: Type definitions without implementation. Libraries ship them or you install via @types/*. Declaration merging adds to existing types.
lessons.q: What is a .d.ts file? When do you write one vs install @types/*? What is the difference between declare module and declare global?
lessons.qsub: How does TypeScript resolve types for an npm package? What is the exports map resolution order? What is skipLibCheck and when is it a trap?
terms: Sirf types wali file — koi chalne wala code nahi.
"Ye cheez kahin aur hai, uska type ye hai".
lessons.what:
Ek file jisme sirf types hote hain, koi code nahi. Ye JavaScript libraries par types "chipkane" ke liye hoti hai.

Aap teen jagah milengi: library ke andar, @types/* package mein, ya aapke apne project mein.
lessons.why: Purani JS libraries mein types nahi hain. .d.ts se aap unhe types de sakte ho bina library chhue. Aur agar aap library banate ho, to declaration: true se ye apne aap ban jaati hai.
where: Purani JS package ko types dena.
pros: Bina library badle types mil jaate hain.
declaration: true se apni library ke types apne aap.
Module augmentation se third-party types extend ho jaate hain.
cons: .d.ts ka koi check nahi hota — galat likha to chup-chaap jhooth.
@types package library se purana ho sakta hai.
Global declarations poore project ko affect karti hain.
gotchas: .d.ts ek waada hai, sach nahi. Aap galat type likh sakte ho aur compiler maan lega — bug chalte waqt milega.
Har Vite/webpack project mein declare module "*.svg" chahiye, warna asset import par error.
declare global sirf module file mein chalta hai (jisme ek import/export ho).

lessons.name: CommonJS vs ESM in TypeScript
lessons.desc: TS compiles to CJS, ESM, or others. Module resolution (how imports are found) is separate from module format (what is emitted). Mixing them causes import errors.
lessons.q: What is the difference between CommonJS and ESM output from TypeScript? What breaks when a CJS consumer requires an ESM package?
lessons.qsub: What is the dual-publish pattern for TypeScript libraries? How do you correctly set up package.json exports to support both CJS and ESM consumers?
terms: TypeScript kaise dhundta hai ki import kahan se aaya.
lessons.what:
TypeScript mein module ka jhanjhat teen settings ka mila-jula nateeja hai: module, moduleResolution, aur package.json ka "type".

Zyadatar "Cannot find module" wali errors inhi teeno ke aapas mein na milne se aati hain.
lessons.why: JavaScript do module systems ke beech mein phansa hua hai. TypeScript ko dono sambhalne padte hain, aur uske liye use batana padta hai ki aapka bundler kaisa behave karta hai.
where: Dono ke liye build karna padta hai.
pros: moduleResolution: "bundler" ne frontend ka jhanjhat lagbhag khatam kar diya.
import type se bundle mein bekaar imports nahi jaate.
esModuleInterop se CommonJS packages seedha import ho jaate hain.
cons: Node ESM mein .js extension likhna ajeeb lagta hai.
CommonJS aur ESM mix karna aaj bhi dard hai.
__dirname jaisi cheezein ESM mein nahi milti.
gotchas: Node ESM mein import path mein .js likhna padta hai, chahe file .ts ho. Ye sabse zyada confuse karne wali baat hai.
"Cannot find module" ka jawab lagbhag hamesha moduleResolution hota hai — pehle wahi dekho.
verbatimModuleSyntax: true on kar lo — usse import type likhna zaroori ho jaata hai aur bundler ki galtiyan bachti hain.

lessons.name: Project References & Incremental Builds
lessons.desc: Split a large monorepo into sub-projects with their own tsconfig. TypeScript builds only what changed using .tsbuildinfo files.
lessons.q: What are TypeScript project references? How do they speed up large monorepo builds? What is composite: true and why is it required?
lessons.qsub: What is the .tsbuildinfo file? How does TypeScript use it for incremental compilation? What breaks if you delete it?
terms: Ek TS project doosre par nirbhar — alag-alag build hote hain.
Sirf badla hua hissa dobara compile karna.
Wo flag jo project ko reference-able banata hai.
lessons.what: Bade repos mein sab kuch ek saath compile karna slow hai. Project references se aap use tukdon mein baant dete ho, aur TypeScript sirf badle hue tukde dobara banata hai.
lessons.why: Monorepo mein ek badlav par poora type-check chalna minutes le sakta hai. References ke saath sirf affected package rebuild hota hai — 2 minute ka build 10 second ka ho jaata hai.
pros: Build bahut tez — sirf badla hua hissa.
Package ki boundary compiler enforce karta hai.
Editor bhi tez ho jaata hai.
cons: Setup ka jhanjhat.
tsc --build use karna yaad rakhna padta hai.
Chhote projects ke liye bekaar.
gotchas: tsc nahi, tsc --build — plain tsc references ko ignore kar deta hai.
composite: true ke saath declaration: true zaroori hai.
Chhote project mein sirf "incremental": true laga do — 80% faayda, zero setup.

lessons.name: TypeScript Compiler API & AST
lessons.desc: TypeScript exposes its compiler as a public API. Used by ESLint, ts-morph, and custom build tools to analyse and transform code.
lessons.q: What is the TypeScript Compiler API? What can you do with it that you cannot do with regular type checking alone?
lessons.qsub: What is an AST in TypeScript? What is the difference between ts.Node, ts.Type, and ts.Symbol? How do tools like ts-morph simplify working with the AST?
terms: TypeScript ko library ki tarah use karna.
Abstract Syntax Tree — code ka tree roop.
lessons.what:
TypeScript sirf ek compiler nahi — ek library bhi hai. Aap use import karke code parse kar sakte ho, uska tree ghoom sakte ho, aur naya code likh sakte ho.

Raw API bhaari hai; ts-morph uska aasan wrapper hai aur zyadatar kaam ke liye wahi use karna chahiye.
lessons.why: Codemods (poore codebase mein ek pattern badalna), custom lint rules, aur code generation — teenon isse hote hain. Aur agar aapne RAG journal kiya hai, to ts-morph se chunking wahi cheez thi.
where: Apne project ke niyam enforce karna.
pros: Poore codebase par safe automated changes.
Type information tak pahunch — regex se ye kabhi nahi hota.
ts-morph se seekhna aasan.
cons: Raw API ka seekhna mushkil hai.
Bade codebase par slow.
Zyadatar developers ko kabhi zarurat nahi padti.
gotchas: Regex se code mat badlo — ts-morph 20 minute mein seekh jaate ho aur wo galtiyan nahi karta.
ts-morph se shuru karo, raw API tab jab wo kaafi na ho.
Ye wahi tool hai jo aapne RAG journal ke Phase 3 mein AST chunking ke liye use kiya tha.

lessons.name: Source Maps & Declaration Maps
lessons.desc: Source maps map compiled JS back to TS for debugging. Declaration maps map .d.ts back to .ts source for IDE go-to-definition. Essential for library authors.
lessons.q: What is the difference between sourceMap and declarationMap? Why should library authors ship declaration maps? How does "go to source" work in node_modules?
lessons.qsub: What happens if you publish a package with declarationMap: true but forget the .ts source files? Can declaration maps point to source files outside the package?
terms: Compiled code ko wapas asli code se jodne wali file.
.d.ts ko asli source se jodne wali file.
lessons.what:
Browser aapka compiled JS chalata hai, par aapko apna TypeScript debug karna hai. Source map wo pull hai jo dono ko jodta hai.

Declaration map alag cheez hai: usse editor mein "Go to Definition" aapko .d.ts ki jagah asli source par le jaata hai.
lessons.why: Bina source maps ke production ka stack trace bundle.min.js:1:48291 jaisa hota hai — bilkul bekaar. Unke saath wo aapki asli file aur line dikhata hai.
pros: Production stack traces padhne layak ho jaate hain.
Breakpoints asli TypeScript par lagte hain.
declarationMap monorepo mein navigation theek kar deta hai.
cons: Public source maps se aapka source sabko dikh jaata hai.
Build size badhta hai.
Sentry mein upload karna ek extra step hai.
gotchas: Source maps public mat karo — Sentry ko upload karo aur public folder se hata do (sourcemap: "hidden").
declarationMap: true monorepo mein sabse under-rated setting hai — Cmd+Click asli source par le jaata hai.
Production errors samajh nahi aa rahe? Pehle check karo ki source maps upload ho rahe hain ya nahi.

lessons.name: JSX & React Configuration
lessons.desc: jsx controls JSX emission: react (React.createElement), react-jsx (_jsx runtime, TS 4.1+), preserve (keep for Babel), react-native. jsxFactory, jsxFragmentFactory for custom runtimes.
lessons.q: What are the TS jsx options and when should you use each? What changed with the automatic JSX runtime (react-jsx) and why is it preferred?
lessons.qsub: What is jsxImportSource? How do you configure a custom JSX pragma for Preact or SolidJS? What happens if jsx is set to "react" but React is not in scope?
terms: Naya transform — import React ki zarurat nahi.
Wo file extension jisme JSX likha ja sakta hai.
lessons.what: Ek setting jo tay karti hai ki JSX kaise compile hoga. Aaj ka sahi jawab "react-jsx" hai.
lessons.why: Purane transform mein har file mein import React from "react" likhna padta tha — chahe aapne React kahin use kiya ho ya nahi. Naya transform wo import khud daal deta hai.
pros: Har file mein import React ki zarurat khatam.
Bundle thoda chhota.
Naye JSX transform se better tree shaking.
cons: .tsx mein generic arrow function ambiguous ho jaata hai.
React 17+ chahiye.
Purane tutorials abhi bhi import React dikhate hain.
gotchas: .tsx mein <T>(x: T) => x nahi chalega — TS ise JSX tag samajh leta hai. <T,> likho (comma ke saath).
React.FC aaj recommend nahi hota — plain function + typed props behtar hai.
"jsx": "preserve" tab jab koi aur tool (Next.js, babel) JSX handle kar raha ho.

lessons.name: Lib, Target & Module Configuration
lessons.desc: target sets the JS language level (ES2015, ES2020, ESNext). lib specifies which ambient declarations to include. module sets the output module system. These three interact.
lessons.q: What is the interaction between target, lib, and module in tsconfig? Why would you set target: ES2015 but lib: ES2023? What does "lib" actually control?
lessons.qsub: Why does target: ES2015 but using Array.from in source NOT cause a compile error (hint: lib)? What is the difference between lib and @types? When should you use --skipLibCheck?
terms: Output JavaScript kis version ka hoga.
lessons.what:
Do settings jo aapas mein juri hain aur aksar confuse karti hain:

target = "output kis JS version mein hoga".
lib = "kaunse built-in types mujhe dikhenge".

target set karne par lib apne aap set ho jaati hai — par aap use override kar sakte ho.
lessons.why: Galat target se do problem hoti hain: bahut purana rakhoge to # private fields slow WeakMap code ban jaate hain; bahut naya rakhoge to purane browsers par crash. Aur galat lib se document jaisi cheezein "not found" dikhne lagti hain.
where: Thoda purana target — zyada logon ke liye chalega.
pros: Sahi target se output chhota aur tez.
lib se galat APIs dikhte hi nahi.
types se node_modules ke types control mein.
cons: lib aur target ka rishta confuse karta hai.
lib naya rakhne se polyfill khud daalna padta hai.
Galat setup ke errors samajhna mushkil.
gotchas: target: "ES2022" rakho — warna # private fields slow WeakMap code mein badal jaate hain.
Node project mein DOM lib mat daalo — warna document autocomplete mein dikhega jo chalte waqt hai hi nahi.
lib sirf types deta hai, polyfill nahi. Naye method ka type mil gaya iska matlab wo purane browser mein chalega nahi.

lessons.name: Path Aliases & Base URL
lessons.desc: paths and baseUrl enable import aliases like @/components/Button instead of ../../../components/Button. Requires matching bundler config (vite, webpack, tsconfig-paths at runtime).
lessons.q: How do you configure path aliases in TypeScript? What is the relationship between baseUrl and paths? Why do path aliases need separate runtime configuration?
lessons.qsub: What is tsconfig-paths and how does it work for Node.js runtime resolution? Why can't TypeScript's paths alone fix runtime module resolution? How does the exports map in package.json interact with TypeScript path aliases?
terms: Wo folder jisse relative paths shuru hote hain.
lessons.what:
../../../utils/format ki jagah @/utils/format likhna.

Par ek zaroori baat: TypeScript sirf type-check ke liye ye samajhta hai. Chalte waqt aapke bundler ko alag se batana padta hai.
lessons.why: ../../../ wale imports file move karte hi toot jaate hain, aur padhne mein bhi bekaar hain. Alias se import path file ki jagah se azaad ho jaata hai.
where: Deep relative imports se bachne ke liye.
File move karne par imports nahi tootte.
pros: Import padhne mein saaf.
File move karne par kuch nahi tootta.
vite-tsconfig-paths se ek hi jagah config.
cons: Do jagah setup karna padta hai — tsconfig aur bundler.
Jest/vitest ko alag se batana padta hai.
Plain Node mein bilkul kaam nahi karta.
gotchas: paths sirf TypeScript ke liye hai. Bundler ko alag se alias batao, warna type-check pass hoga aur chalte waqt "module not found" milega.
vite-tsconfig-paths plugin laga lo — phir sirf tsconfig mein likhna kaafi hai.
Test runner ko alag se batana bhoolna aam hai — test fail honge par app chalega.

lessons.name: Typing React Components & Props
lessons.desc: React.FC adds implicit children and restricts generics. Explicit typed functions give more control. PropsWithChildren adds children explicitly.
lessons.q: What is the difference between React.FC<Props> and a plain typed function? Why do many teams avoid React.FC? What problems does it cause?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, and ReactChild? Which should you use for a children prop and why?
terms: Component ko diya gaya data — ek normal object.
Kuch bhi jo render ho sakta hai — JSX, string, number, array, null.
Purana tarika props type karne ka. Aaj recommend nahi hota.
lessons.what:
React component ek normal function hai jo ek object leta hai. To use type karna bhi normal function type karne jaisa hai — koi khaas React jaadu nahi.

Return type likhne ki zarurat bhi nahi — TypeScript JSX se khud pehchan leta hai.
lessons.why: React.FC pehle standard tha, par uske do nuksaan the: wo children chup-chaap de deta tha (chahe aapka component use na leta ho), aur generic components ke saath kaam nahi karta. React 18 mein pehla theek ho gaya, par tab tak team plain function par shift ho chuki thi — aur wahi aaj ka sahi jawab hai.
where: Doosre component ke props extend karna.
pros: Props galat dena compile time par pakda jaata hai.
ComponentProps se native HTML props muft mein.
Autocomplete se component use karna aasan.
cons: React.FC vs plain function ka confusion abhi bhi hai.
Purane tutorials galat tarika dikhate hain.
ReactNode vs ReactElement ka farak yaad rakhna padta hai.
gotchas: React.FC mat use karo — plain function + typed props. Ye aaj ka standard hai.
children ab apne aap nahi milta (React 18 se) — chahiye to children?: React.ReactNode khud likho.
ComponentProps<"button"> ek bahut under-rated trick hai — 30 native props ek line mein.

lessons.name: Typing Hooks
lessons.desc: useState infers from initial value. useRef has two overloads: DOM ref (HTMLElement | null) and mutable ref (MutableRefObject<T>). useReducer needs explicit action types.
lessons.q: When does TypeScript infer useState<T> correctly vs when must you annotate? Show 3 common useState typing mistakes in real code.
lessons.qsub: What are the two overloads of useRef and when does each apply? How do you correctly type a ref that will be attached to a DOM element?
terms: TypeScript khud type pehchan le — zyadatar hooks mein yahi hota hai.
lessons.what:
Zyadatar hooks ko type karne ki zarurat hi nahi — initial value se TypeScript sab samajh leta hai.

Type sirf teen jagah likhna padta hai: jab initial value null ho, jab wo khaali array ho, aur jab shuruaat mein pata na ho ki aage kya aayega.
lessons.why: Sabse aam bug: useState(null) ka type null ban jaata hai — phir usme user daalne par error. Aur useState([]) ka type never[] ban jaata hai, jisme kuch push hi nahi kar sakte.
pros: Zyadatar jagah inference se kaam ho jaata hai.
useReducer + union se har action type-safe.
useRef se DOM access safe.
cons: useState(null) aur useState([]) ke traps.
useRef ke do alag roop confuse karte hain.
Generic custom hooks likhna thoda mushkil hai.
gotchas: useState([]) ka type never[] ban jaata hai — kuch push hi nahi kar paoge. useState<Item[]>([]) likho.
useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null) — DOM ref ke liye null initial value zaroori hai, warna type readonly ban jaata hai.
useReducer ke saath action ko discriminated union banao — har case mein sirf uske apne fields milenge.

lessons.name: Typing Event Handlers
lessons.desc: React wraps native events in SyntheticEvent. Each element type has specific event types: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>, React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>.
lessons.q: What is the difference between React.ChangeEvent, React.FormEvent, and React.MouseEvent? How do you type a generic onChange handler that works across input types?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between React.SyntheticEvent and the native DOM Event? How do you access the native event when you need it?
terms: React ka apna event wrapper — native event jaisa par cross-browser.
lessons.what:
React events native events nahi hain — wo React ke apne wrapper hain. Isliye unke types bhi React se aate hain, DOM se nahi.

Aur ek chhota trick: agar handler seedha JSX mein likha ho, to type likhne ki zarurat hi nahi — React khud bata deta hai.
lessons.why: Sahi event type se aapko e.target.value par autocomplete milta hai. Galat type par ya to any milta hai ya "property does not exist" — aur log phir as any laga dete hain, jo poora point khatam kar deta hai.
pros: Inline handlers ko type karne ki zarurat hi nahi.
e.target.value par poora autocomplete.
currentTarget ka type hamesha sahi hota hai.
cons: Type ke naam lambe hain aur yaad nahi rehte.
target vs currentTarget confuse karta hai.
Alag element ke liye alag generic likhna padta hai.
gotchas: Inline handler ko type mat likho — React khud bata deta hai. Sirf alag function ke liye likho.
e.target ka type EventTarget hota hai (chauda), e.currentTarget ka exact — form mein hamesha currentTarget.
Checkbox mein e.target.checked chahiye, value nahi — ye classic galti hai.

lessons.name: Generic Components
lessons.desc: Components that accept type parameters — for typed lists, tables, selects. Arrow function generics in .tsx files clash with JSX angle brackets.
lessons.q: How do you write a generic React component? Implement a typed List<T> component with a typed renderItem prop and keyExtractor.
lessons.qsub: What is the TSX angle bracket ambiguity problem with generic arrow functions? What are the two solutions and which is preferred?
terms: Aisa component jo kisi bhi type ke data ke saath chale, type khoye bina.
lessons.what:
Ek List component jo User[] bhi le sake aur Product[] bhi — aur render function mein sahi type de sake.

any se ye kaam chal jaata hai, par tab renderItem ke andar autocomplete khatam.
lessons.why: Ye wahi jagah hai jahan React.FC fail karta hai — usme generic likhne ka koi tarika hi nahi. Isliye plain function hi ek matra raasta hai.
where: Har data type ke liye ek hi component.
pros: Ek component, har data type.
Render callbacks mein poora type safety.
Constraint se zaroori fields pakke.
cons: .tsx mein arrow function ke saath <T,> ka jugaad.
React.FC ke saath kaam hi nahi karta.
Zyada generics padhne mein bhaari.
gotchas: .tsx mein <T> arrow function JSX samjha jaata hai — <T,> likho ya function declaration use karo.
Generic components React.FC ke saath likhe hi nahi ja sakte — yahi uska sabse bada nuksaan hai.
Callback props (renderItem) ke andar autocomplete aana hi is poore kaam ka nateeja hai — wo nahi aa raha to generic sahi nahi laga.

lessons.name: Typing Context
lessons.desc: createContext requires a default. Using undefined as default with a custom assertion hook avoids casting everywhere while keeping TypeScript happy.
lessons.q: What is the best pattern for typing React Context with TypeScript? Why is createContext<T | undefined>(undefined) + a custom hook better than createContext<T>(staleDefault)?
lessons.qsub: How do you create a context + hook pattern where TypeScript knows the value is always defined inside the Provider without using non-null assertion (!) everywhere?
terms: Bina props drilling ke data neeche pahunchana.
lessons.what:
Context ka type karna aasan hai — par ek jagah sab phansteे hain: default value kya do?

Do raaste hain, aur dusra kaafi behtar hai.
lessons.why: Agar aap createContext<User | null>(null) likhte ho, to har component mein if (!user) return likhna padta hai — jabki asal mein Provider hamesha hota hai. Custom hook wale tarike se wo check ek jagah aa jaata hai.
pros: Custom hook se null check ek jagah.
Galat use par saaf error message.
Poora value type-safe.
cons: useMemo bhoolne par har render sab consumers ko re-render.
Bade context frequent re-render banate hain.
Testing ke liye provider wrap karna padta hai.
gotchas: Provider ka value hamesha useMemo mein rakho — warna har render par naya object banta hai aur saare consumers re-render hote hain.
Custom hook (useAuth) hamesha banao — usme throw se null check ek hi jagah aa jaata hai.
Ek bade context ki jagah do chhote banao (state aur dispatch alag) — jise sirf dispatch chahiye wo state badalne par re-render nahi hoga.

lessons.name: Typing forwardRef & useImperativeHandle
lessons.desc: forwardRef<Ref, Props> needs explicit type params. useImperativeHandle constrains what the parent can access via the ref handle.
lessons.q: What is the exact type signature of React.forwardRef? Why do you need to annotate both the ref type and the props type explicitly?
lessons.qsub: How do you type useImperativeHandle to expose only a focus() method while internally holding a ref to the full HTMLInputElement?
terms: Parent ka ref child ke andar ke DOM element tak pahunchana.
Ref ke through custom methods bahar dena.
lessons.what:
Normally ref component ko nahi milta — wo React ka reserved prop hai. forwardRef se aap use aage pass kar sakte ho.

Aur useImperativeHandle se aap DOM node ki jagah apne methods bahar de sakte ho.
lessons.why:
Design system mein ye zaroori hai — aapka <Input /> ek wrapper hai, par user ko inputRef.current.focus() chalana hai. Bina forwardRef ke wo ref kahin nahi pahunchta.

Note: React 19 mein ref ek normal prop ban gaya hai — to naye code mein forwardRef ki zarurat kam ho rahi hai. Par har existing codebase mein ye milega.
where: react-hook-form ko ref chahiye hota hai.
pros: Wrapper components ke saath ref kaam karta hai.
useImperativeHandle se controlled imperative API.
Poora type-safe.
cons: forwardRef<Ref, Props> ka ulta order confuse karta hai.
Imperative APIs React ki soch ke khilaaf hain — kam use karo.
React 19 mein purana ho raha hai.
gotchas: Generic ka order ulta hai: forwardRef<RefType, PropsType> — pehle ref, phir props. Ye sabse aam galti hai.
Andar wale function ko naam do, warna React DevTools mein "Anonymous" dikhega.
useImperativeHandle se pehle sochо — zyadatar cases props se ho jaate hain, aur wo React ka sahi tarika hai.

lessons.name: Typing State Management (Redux / Zustand)
lessons.desc: Redux requires typing actions (discriminated unions), reducers, and selectors. Zustand uses infer and generic stores. Both benefit from typed middleware.
lessons.q: How do you type a Redux reducer with discriminated union actions? What is the pattern for typing createSlice (RTK) to get typed actions and state?
lessons.qsub: How does Zustand use TypeScript inference to create typed stores without explicit type annotations? How do you type Zustand middleware (persist, immer, devtools)?
terms: Poore app ki state ek jagah.
Store se ek tukda nikalne wala function.
lessons.what:
Redux Toolkit aur Zustand dono inference-first hain — aap types likhte nahi, nikalte ho.

State ka shape store se nikalta hai, aur wo kabhi purana nahi hota.
lessons.why: Purane Redux mein action types, reducers aur state shapes teenon alag likhne padte the — aur teeno sync rakhne padte the. RTK mein aap sirf ek jagah likhte ho aur baaki ReturnType se nikal jaate hain.
where: React Query — ye alag cheez hai, iske liye behtar.
pros: Types nikalte hain — likhne ki zarurat nahi.
RTK ka Immer se mutate-jaisa likhna aasan.
Typed hooks ek baar banao, poore app mein.
cons: RTK ka setup thoda bhaari hai.
Selector na dena har badlav par re-render karta hai.
Log server data bhi global store mein daal dete hain — wo galat jagah hai.
gotchas: Store se type nikalo, likho mat — ReturnType<typeof store.getState>. Ye pattern dono libraries mein same hai.
Zustand mein hamesha selector do (useStore(s => s.count)) — poora store lene par har badlav re-render karta hai.
Server se aaya data global store mein mat daalo — React Query use karo. Wo caching, refetch aur stale handling khud karta hai.

lessons.name: Typing Custom Hooks with Generics
lessons.desc: Custom hooks often need generics for flexibility — useFetch<T>, useLocalStorage<T>, useDebounce<T>. Generic hooks propagate types from input to output seamlessly.
lessons.q: Design a typed useFetch<T> hook that takes a URL, returns { data: T | null, loading: boolean, error: Error | null }. How does the generic flow from caller to return type?
lessons.qsub: How do you type useLocalStorage<T> with a default value to handle SSR (server-side rendering) where localStorage is undefined? How does the generic constraint work with JSON serialization?
terms: Ek function jo use se shuru ho aur andar hooks use kare.
Tuple return ko lock karna — taaki destructuring sahi type de.
lessons.what: Custom hook ek normal function hai. Uska type karna bhi normal hai — ek cheez chhod kar: agar aap tuple (array) return kar rahe ho, to as const lagana padta hai.
lessons.why: Bina as const ke return [value, setValue] ka type (T | Function)[] ban jaata hai — dono positions par union. Phir destructure karne par value bhi function ho sakta hai, aur autocomplete khatam.
pros: Logic reuse aur poori type safety.
Generic hooks se ek hi hook har type ke liye.
Result union se impossible states khatam.
cons: Tuple return ke saath as const bhoolna aam hai.
Generic hooks likhna shuru mein mushkil.
Zyada abstraction se debugging mushkil.
gotchas: Tuple return karo to as const zaroori hai — warna dono positions par union type aa jaata hai aur destructuring bekaar ho jaati hai.
Do se zyada cheezein return karni hon to object do, tuple nahi — naam se pata chalta hai kya hai.
Loading/error/data ko alag flags ki jagah discriminated union banao — "loading true aur data bhi hai" jaisi asambhav haalat likhi hi nahi ja sakegi.

lessons.name: Typing Polymorphic Components
lessons.desc: A component that renders as different HTML elements (as prop — <Button as="a" />). Requires complex generic props merging with proper type narrowing.
lessons.q: What is a polymorphic component in React + TypeScript? Implement Button with an as prop that correctly types the additional props based on the chosen element.
lessons.qsub: What is the PolymorphicComponentProps pattern with AsProp and OwnProps? How do you handle the ref type changing when the as element changes? What are the limitations of the Pattern ('as' prop + rest props union)?
terms: Aisa component jo as prop se koi bhi HTML element ban sake.
lessons.what:
Ek <Text> component jo as="h1" ya as="a" ya as={Link} ban sake — aur har case mein us element ke sahi props le sake.

Yahi aakhri hissa mushkil hai: as="a" par href milna chahiye, as="button" par nahi.
lessons.why: Design systems mein ye pattern har jagah hai (Chakra, MUI, Radix). Par imaandari se: iske types likhna TypeScript ka sabse mushkil kaam hai, aur zyadatar apps ko iski zarurat nahi hoti — do-teen alag components aksar behtar hain.
where: Chakra, MUI, Radix — sab yahi karte hain.
Ek Text component, har heading level.
pros: Ek component, har element.
Semantic HTML aur styling alag ho jaate hain.
Library users ke liye bahut flexible.
cons: Types padhne aur likhne mein sabse mushkil.
Error messages lagbhag samajh se bahar.
ref ke saath aur bhi complex.
gotchas: Ye library-level pattern hai. Apne app mein teen simple components aksar behtar hain.
Omit<..., keyof P | "as"> zaroori hai — warna aapke props aur element ke props takra jaate hain.
Interview mein iska naam aur trade-off bata dena kaafi hai — poora type likhwana bahut kam poocha jaata hai.

lessons.name: Discriminated Unions & Exhaustive Checks
lessons.desc: Union types with a shared literal discriminant. TypeScript narrows each branch in a switch. Assigning to never at the end enforces exhaustiveness.
lessons.q: What is a discriminated union? Build an exhaustive check pattern using never that causes a compile error when a new union member is added.
lessons.qsub: What is the never type conceptually? How does assigning an unhandled case to a never variable enforce compile-time exhaustiveness checking?
terms: Wo common literal field jiski value se pata chale ki kaunsa member hai.
Compiler se pakka karwana ki koi case chhoota nahi.
Aisa type jiski koi value ho hi nahi sakti.
lessons.what:
Ek union jiske har member mein ek common field ho jiski value alag ho — status, kind, type.

Us field ko check karte hi TypeScript baaki poora shape jaan leta hai.
lessons.why: Ye TypeScript ka sabse zyada kaam ka pattern hai. Isse "asambhav haalatein" likhi hi nahi ja sakti — loading: true ke saath data hona namumkin ho jaata hai. Aur naya case add karne par compiler har jagah yaad dila deta hai.

visual.cap: Alag flags se 8 combinations bante hain jinme se 5 asambhav hain. Union se sirf 3 valid haalatein rehti hain — aur galat likhna namumkin ho jaata hai.

Narrowing apne aap — as ki zarurat nahi.
Exhaustive check se naya case bhoolna namumkin.
cons: Flags se thoda zyada likhna padta hai.
Discriminant field har member mein chahiye.
Bade unions ke error messages lambe.
gotchas: Discriminant literal hona chahiye — status: string se narrowing kaam nahi karegi, status: "loading" se karegi.
const _never: never = s wala exhaustive check zaroor lagao — wahi naya case bhoolne se bachata hai.
Ye TypeScript ka sabse zyada faayda dene wala pattern hai. Agar ek hi cheez yaad rakhni ho, to yahi.

lessons.name: Branded / Nominal Types
lessons.desc: Add a phantom brand property to make structurally identical types incompatible — prevents accidentally passing a UserId where an OrderId is expected.
lessons.q: What is a branded type? Implement UserId and OrderId that are both strings but not assignable to each other without an explicit cast.
lessons.qsub: What are the tradeoffs of branded types vs using classes for nominal types? How do brands survive JSON serialization and deserialization?
terms: Ek hi shape wali do cheezon ko alag banane ka jugaad.
Ek nakli field jo sirf types mein hota hai, chalte waqt nahi.
lessons.what:
TypeScript structural hai — UserId aur PostId dono string hain, to unhe ek hi maanta hai. Galat id pass karna pakda hi nahi jaata.

Branding ek jugaad hai jisse aap unhe alag bana dete ho — ek nakli field jodkar jo chalte waqt hota hi nahi.
lessons.why: Id mix-up wale bugs bahut mehngey hote hain — getUser(postId) compile ho jaata hai aur production mein galat data deta hai. Branding se wo likhte waqt pakda jaata hai, aur runtime par zero cost hai.
where: Cents vs Rupees — classic mehnga bug.
pros: Id mix-up compile time par pakda jaata hai.
Chalte waqt zero cost — brand gayab ho jaata hai.
Underlying type ke saare methods chalte rehte hain.
cons: Banane ke liye as lagana padta hai (par ek hi jagah).
Bahut sare brands se code shor ban jaata hai.
Third-party types ke saath jodne mein dikkat.
gotchas: as sirf ek jagah — validator function mein. Agar poore codebase mein as UserId likhne lage, to poora faayda khatam.
unique symbol use karo brand key ke liye — string key doosre brand se takra sakti hai.
Cents vs Rupees wala use case sabse zyada paise bachata hai — money handle kar rahe ho to zaroor lagao.

lessons.name: Builder Pattern with Type Tracking
lessons.desc: Method chaining where TypeScript tracks which methods have been called via phantom type parameters — build() is only allowed after required setters.
lessons.q: How do you use TypeScript generics to enforce that a Builder has had all required methods called before .build() is allowed?
lessons.qsub: What is the phantom type approach to builder validation? Show how TypeScript produces a compile error if .setName() has not been called before .build().
terms: Har kadam par type badalna, taaki compiler yaad rakhe kya set ho chuka hai.
lessons.what:
Normal builder chalta hai par ek problem hai: .build() tab bhi bulaya ja sakta hai jab zaroori fields set na hue hon.

Type tracking se har .set() return type badal deta hai — aur .build() tabhi milta hai jab sab zaroori cheezein set ho chuki hon.
lessons.why: Ye TypeScript ka wo istemaal hai jo chalte waqt ki galti ko likhte waqt le aata hai. "Aapne url set nahi kiya" ek runtime error hai — type tracking se wo compile error ban jaata hai.
where: Users ko galat order se rokna.
pros: Runtime error compile error ban jaata hai.
Autocomplete sirf agla valid step dikhata hai.
Documentation ki zarurat kam — types khud batate hain.
cons: Andar as any lagana padta hai.
Error messages confusing.
Simple cases ke liye bahut zyada hai.
gotchas: this parameter wala trick hi asli jaadu hai — build(this: Builder<"url" | "method">).
Andar as any lagana padega — wo theek hai, kyunki bahar ka type poori tarah safe rehta hai.
Simple builder ke liye ye zarurat nahi — object parameter aksar kaafi hai.

lessons.name: Module Augmentation & Declaration Merging
lessons.desc: Extend third-party type definitions without modifying node_modules — add a user property to Express Request, or custom methods to String.prototype.
lessons.q: What is module augmentation? How do you add a user: User property to Express's Request interface so TypeScript knows it everywhere?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between module augmentation (adding to existing) and declaration merging (merging two interfaces)? Which works for classes?
terms: Doosri library ke types mein apna kuch jodna.
Do ek naam ke interface ka apne aap jud jaana.
lessons.what:
Third-party library ke types mein aap apne fields jod sakte ho — bina library chhue.

Ye interface ke merging behaviour se hota hai — wahi cheez jo aapke apne code mein bug hai, yahan feature hai.
lessons.why: Express ka Request mein req.user nahi hota, par aapka auth middleware use daalta hai. Bina augmentation ke aapko har jagah (req as any).user likhna padta.
pros: Library ke types badle bina extend ho jaate hain.
as any ki zarurat khatam.
Env vars type-safe aur autocomplete ke saath.
cons: Sirf interface ke saath kaam karta hai.
Global augmentation poore project par lagti hai.
Waada hai, check nahi — galat likha to chup-chaap jhooth.
gotchas: declare global sirf module file mein chalta hai — file mein kam se kam ek import ya export hona chahiye.
Ye ek waada hai — req.user ko optional (?) rakho, warna type kehta rahega ki hai aur middleware na chalne par undefined milega.
type merge nahi hota, sirf interface — isliye library types aksar interface mein hote hain.

lessons.name: satisfies Operator & Type Validation
lessons.desc: satisfies (TS 4.9) checks that an expression matches a type WITHOUT widening it — you keep literal types AND get shape validation simultaneously.
lessons.q: What does the satisfies operator do that a type annotation or as cast cannot? Give a concrete example where it gives better autocomplete AND type safety.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between x = {a:1} as Config, x: Config = {a:1}, and x = {a:1} satisfies Config? When does each widen vs preserve literal types?
terms: Type check karo, par asli (narrow) type khone mat do.
lessons.what:
Ek nayi cheez (TS 4.9) jo ek purani chidh theek karti hai.

: Type lagane se check hota hai par type chauda ho jaata hai. as Type se check hota hi nahi. satisfies dono deta hai — check bhi, aur asli narrow type bhi.
lessons.why: Config objects mein ye roz kaam aata hai: aapko chahiye ki shape check ho (koi galat key na ho) aur keys ka exact union bhi mile. Pehle dono ek saath mumkin nahi tha.

visual.cap: Teeno ka farak ek hi example par. satisfies check bhi karta hai aur exact type bhi deta hai — isliye config objects mein wahi sahi jawab hai.

Extra keys aur galat values dono pakde jaate hain.
as const ke saath mila kar sabse strong.
cons: TS 4.9+ chahiye.
Log as aur satisfies confuse karte hain.
Purane codebase mein nahi milega.
gotchas: Config objects mein hamesha satisfies, : nahi — warna keys ka exact union nahi milta.
as const satisfies X — dono ek saath lagane par sabse strong result milta hai.
Interview mein "as aur satisfies mein farak" achha sawaal hai: as check hi nahi karta, satisfies karta hai aur type narrow rakhta hai.

lessons.name: Template Literal Types for API Safety
lessons.desc: Combine template literals with mapped types to create type-safe event names, CSS-in-TS, path routers, and API method generators.
lessons.q: Build a type-safe EventEmitter where event names must match "on${Capitalize<EventName>}" and each event name has a specific typed handler signature.
lessons.qsub: How do you extract segments from a URL path type like "/users/:id/posts/:postId" to produce a Params type { id: string; postId: string }?
terms: String types jod kar naya string type banana.
lessons.what:
Template literal types ka asli use — API routes aur event names ko type-safe banana.

Sabse impressive: route string se uske parameters nikal lena.
lessons.why: Route strings sabse aam typo ki jagah hain, aur wo galti chalte waqt milti hai (404). Types se wo likhte waqt pakdi jaati hai — aur params bhoolna bhi.
pros: Route typo compile time par pakda jaata hai.
Params ka naam aur ginti dono check hoti hai.
Editor autocomplete deta hai.
cons: Recursive extraction padhne mein bhaari.
Combination explosion se compiler slow.
Error messages bhaari.
gotchas: ExtractParams jaisa recursive type khud likhne se pehle dekho ki router library (TanStack Router) ye pehle se de rahi ho.
Combination explosion asli problem hai — chaar 5-member unions se 625 types, aur editor slow.
Ye pattern interview mein bahut impress karta hai — ek chhota ExtractParams yaad rakh lo.

lessons.name: Type-Safe Builder & Fluent API Pattern
lessons.desc: Use phantom types and method chaining to enforce compile-time constraints on builder calls. A build() method is only callable after required setters.
lessons.q: Design a type-safe URL builder where setProtocol() and setHost() must be called before build() compiles. Use phantom type parameters to track state.
lessons.qsub: What are the alternatives to phantom types for type-safe builders? How would discriminated unions work instead? What are the trade-offs?
terms: Method chaining — har method khud ko wapas deta hai.
Aisa type parameter jo sirf state track kare, koi value na rakhe.
lessons.what:
Builder pattern ka fluent roop — db.from("users").where(...).select(...).

Aur type tracking se har step ka return type badalta hai, jisse autocomplete sirf agla valid step dikhata hai.
lessons.why: Achhi fluent API ka nishaan ye hai ki galat order likha hi na ja sake. .execute() se pehle .from() zaroori — aur ye documentation se nahi, types se enforce hona chahiye.
pros: Galat order likha hi nahi ja sakta.
Autocomplete sirf valid agla step dikhata hai.
API self-documenting ban jaati hai.
cons: Andar as any chahiye.
Debug karna mushkil.
App code mein aksar over-engineering.
gotchas: Poore type tracking se pehle poochho: "kya order sach mein maayne rakhta hai?" Nahi to object parameter kaafi hai.
this parameter (execute(this: Query<{table: string}>)) hi wo trick hai jo method ko conditionally available banati hai.
Ye library-level pattern hai — Prisma/Kysely padho, ye poora isi tarah bana hai.

lessons.name: Type-Safe Event Emitter Pattern
lessons.desc: Generic Event Emitter where each event name has a typed payload. Uses mapped types + template literals to enforce event name → payload mapping.
lessons.q: Design a typed EventEmitter<T> where T is a map of event names to payloads. Implement on(event, handler) and emit(event, payload) with full type safety.
lessons.qsub: How do you handle off() (removing a listener) with type safety? What is the pattern for once()? How do you support { once?: boolean } in the options?
terms: Ek type jo batata hai ki kaunse event ka payload kya hai.
lessons.what:
Normal event emitter mein event ka naam ek string hota hai aur payload any — to typo aur galat payload dono chup-chaap nikal jaate hain.

Ek event map type se dono pakde jaate hain.
lessons.why: Event-driven code mein sabse aam bug yahi hai: emit karte waqt event ka naam thoda alag likh diya, aur listener kabhi chala hi nahi — koi error nahi, bas feature kaam nahi karta.
pros: Event naam ka typo compile time par pakda jaata hai.
Payload ka shape har event ke liye alag aur check hota hai.
Listener mein poora autocomplete.
cons: Event map maintain karna padta hai.
Generic code padhne mein thoda bhaari.
Dynamic event names ke saath kaam nahi karta.
gotchas: Har listener ko try/catch mein lapetо — warna ek buggy listener baaki sabko rok dega.
on() se unsubscribe function wapas do — cleanup bhoolna memory leak hai.
Ye pattern WebSocket messages ke liye bhi bilkul waisa hi kaam karta hai — ek map, poori safety.

lessons.name: Assertion Functions Pattern
lessons.desc: Functions that throw to narrow types. Used at runtime to assert invariants and let TypeScript narrow from the caller's perspective. Cleaner than if (!x) throw.
lessons.q: Design assertDefined, assertInstanceOf, and assertShape functions with proper asserts return types. How do they compose with other type guards?
lessons.qsub: How do assertion functions interact with the control flow analyzer? Can you chain assertions? What happens if you wrap an assertion in a try/catch — does TypeScript still narrow?
terms: Galat hone par throw kare, aur uske baad type maan liya jaaye.
Aisi baat jo is point par pakka sach honi chahiye.
lessons.what:
Syntax ("Assertion Functions" lesson mein) jaanne ke baad asli sawaal ye hai: use kahan karna hai.

Teen jagah hain jahan ye if se saaf aur ! se safe hai.
lessons.why: ! compiler ko chup karata hai par check karta hi nahi — crash par sirf "cannot read properties of null" milta hai. Assertion function asli check karta hai aur saaf message deta hai.
where: Env vars, config — galat ho to app chalna hi nahi chahiye.
pros: if ki nesting khatam.
! se behtar — asli check aur saaf message.
assertNever se naya case bhoolna namumkin.
cons: Arrow function ke saath likha hi nahi ja sakta.
Throw karta hai — recoverable cases ke liye galat.
Return type likhna zaroori hai (inference nahi chalta).
gotchas: Do helpers bana lo — assertDefined aur assertNever — aur ! ki zarurat lagbhag khatam ho jaayegi.
Sirf tab use karo jab galat hona bug ho. Normal cases (user ne khaali form bheja) ke liye return/if.
assertNever exhaustive check ka sabse saaf tarika hai — const _n: never = x se behtar padhta hai.

lessons.name: Mixins — class composition patterns in TypeScript
lessons.desc: Mixins compose class behavior from multiple sources. TypeScript pattern: create a type with constructor signature, write a function returning a class extending the base. Different from interfaces (can have state) and abstract classes (composable).
lessons.q: How do you implement mixins in TypeScript? How do they differ from multiple inheritance?
lessons.qsub: What is the constructor type pattern for mixins? How do you use `applyMixins` helper function?
terms: Behaviour ka tukda jise kai classes mein mila diya jaaye.
lessons.what:
TypeScript mein ek class ka ek hi baap ho sakta hai. Mixin uska jugaad hai: ek function jo class leta hai aur usse extend karke nayi class lautata hai.

Phir aap unhe chain kar sakte ho.
lessons.why: Kai jagah se code chahiye (sirf waada nahi, to interface kaafi nahi) — timestamps, serialization, events. Mixin se combination banana jodne jaisa ho jaata hai, nayi class banane jaisa nahi.
pros: Ek baap ki limit se bachaata hai.
Chain karke combinations bana sakte ho.
TypeScript ise poori tarah type kar leta hai.
cons: Naam takraav chup-chaap hota hai.
Types padhne mein bhaari.
"Ye method aaya kahan se" dhundhna mushkil.
gotchas: type Ctor<T> = new (...args: any[]) => T — ye ek line poore mixin pattern ka aadhaar hai.
Do mixins mein ek hi method ka naam ho to baad wala chup-chaap jeet jaata hai — koi error nahi.
Pehle composition sochо (field mein object rakhna) — wo padhne mein saaf hai aur naam takrata nahi.

lessons.name: TypeScript with Jest & Vitest
lessons.desc: Jest needs ts-jest or @swc/jest for transformation. Vitest has built-in TypeScript support via esbuild. Both require tsconfig matching for path aliases.
lessons.q: What is the difference between configuring Jest with ts-jest vs @swc/jest? Why does Vitest not need a separate TypeScript compilation step?
lessons.qsub: How do you configure Vitest to respect tsconfig paths? What is the difference between transforming TypeScript for tests (esbuild/swc) vs running tsc? Which catches type errors?
terms: TS ko JS mein badalna taaki test runner chala sake
wo tools jo transpile ka kaam karte hain — SWC/esbuild fast, ts-jest slow par type-check karta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Jest aur Vitest JavaScript test runners hain. TypeScript ko chalane ke liye unhe pehle TS → JS transpile chahiye, ya to ts-jest se ya SWC/esbuild se.

Yaad rakho — test runner type-check nahi karta. Vo sirf types hata ke code chala deta hai. Type errors alag se tsc --noEmit se pakde jaate hain.
lessons.analogy: Test runner ek driver hai jo gaadi chalata hai. Types gaadi ke design blueprint hain. Driver blueprint nahi padhta — vo bas chalata hai. Blueprint check karne ke liye alag engineer (tsc) chahiye.
lessons.why: Bina setup ke import { add } from './math' chalte hi SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement ya Unexpected token : milega. Vitest mein ye setup already built-in hai (Vite esbuild se transpile karta hai), isliye TS projects mein Vitest ka setup 2 line ka hai aur Jest ka 20 line ka.

Vitest default choice — config almost zero
ts-jest ya @swc/jest se TS support add karte hain
pros: Test file mein bhi autocomplete aur type safety milti hai
Vitest mein setup lagbhag zero — Vite hi transpile kar deta hai
Refactor karo to test file bhi red ho jaati hai — bug pakda jaata hai
cons: ts-jest slow hai kyunki har file type-check karta hai
Do commands maintain karni padti hain (test + typecheck)
Config galat ho to error message confusing hote hain
gotchas: Test pass hona type-safe hone ka proof NAHI hai — CI mein tsc --noEmit zaroor rakho
ts-jest ka isolatedModules:true fast to karta hai par type-check band kar deta hai
tsconfig mein "types": ["vitest/globals"] bhoole to describe/it par red squiggle aayega

lessons.name: Type-Level Testing (tsd / vitest)
lessons.desc: TypeScript lacks built-in type tests. tsd and vitest's expectTypeOf provide assertion-based type testing. Catch type regressions during CI without running a compiler.
lessons.q: What tools exist for testing TypeScript types? How does expectTypeOf<string> work under the hood? Write tests for: Equal, NotEqual, and Extends type assertions.
lessons.qsub: How do you test that a generic function returns the correct type for different inputs? What is the "type test" convention for libraries like Zod and React Query?
terms: test jo runtime pe kuch nahi chalata — sirf check karta hai type sahi nikla ya nahi
jaan-boojh ke galat code likhna aur check karna ki TS ne error diya
lessons.what:
Definition: Type-level testing yaani apne types ke liye tests likhna. Normal test check karta hai value sahi hai; type test check karta hai type sahi hai.

Tools: expectTypeOf (Vitest built-in), tsd, ya khud ka Expect<Equal<A,B>> helper.
lessons.analogy: Normal test: "kek ka swaad theek hai?" Type test: "recipe mein sahi ingredients likhe hain?" Recipe galat ho to kek toh ban jaayega, par agli baar galat banega.
lessons.why: Jab tum ek generic utility likhte ho — Pick, ek builder, ek API client — to uska sabse bada value uska type inference hai. Agar galti se inference any ho gaya, runtime test fir bhi pass ho jaayega, par saare users ka type safety chup-chaap khatam ho jaayega. Sirf type test hi ye pakadta hai.
where: apni npm package ke public types lock karne ke liye
complex conditional/mapped type likhne ke baad
response type sahi infer ho raha hai ye pakka karne ko
pros: Silent any-leak pakadta hai jo runtime test kabhi nahi pakdega
Refactor ke waqt type contract todne par turant fail
Documentation ki tarah kaam karta hai — expected type saaf dikhta hai
cons: Sirf apne code ke liye worth hai — har function ke liye nahi
Equal<> helper ke edge cases hain (any vs unknown weird behave karte hain)
Error messages "true is not assignable to false" jaise cryptic hote hain
gotchas: @ts-expect-error tabhi valid hai jab error AAYE — agar error hat gaya to ye khud error de dega (ye achha hai)
toEqualTypeOf strict hai; toMatchTypeOf loose — dono ka farak samjho
any kisi bhi type ke saath "equal" nahi hota Equal<> helper mein — isliye any-leak turant dikhta hai

lessons.name: Typing Mocks & Test Fixtures
lessons.desc: jest.mock and vi.mock create typed mocks. jest.Mocked<T> and vi.Mocked<T> wrap the original type with mock functions. Partial mocks require explicit type alignment.
lessons.q: How does jest.Mocked<T> work? What is the difference between jest.mock('module') auto-mocking and manual __mocks__ with type assertions?
lessons.qsub: How do you create a factory function for typed test fixtures (using Partial<T> + defaults)? How does the satisfies operator improve factory typing?
terms: asli function ki jagah nakli function jo tum control karte ho
test ke liye banaya gaya sample data object
poore object ka sirf kuch hissa nakli banana
lessons.what:
Definition: Mock = asli dependency (API call, DB, timer) ko test mein nakli version se replace karna. TypeScript mein challenge ye hai ki nakli version ka type asli jaisa hona chahiye, warna type safety chali jaati hai.

Do tools: vi.mocked(fn) jo mock ko typed banata hai, aur Partial<T> + factory function fixtures ke liye.
lessons.why: Sabse aam galti: const mockUser = {} as User. Ye compile ho jaata hai par jab User mein naya required field aayega, ye test chup-chaap galat data ke saath pass hota rahega. Typed factory se aisa nahi hota.
where: network call ki jagah fixed response
har test mein 10-field object likhne ki jagah factory
DB, filesystem, clock ko replace karne ke liye
pros: vi.mocked se mockResolvedValue par bhi type-check milta hai
Factory pattern se User mein naya field add karte hi ek jagah fix karna padta hai
Partial<T> override se test mein sirf relevant field dikhta hai — readable
cons: Zyada mocking se test asli behaviour test karna band kar deta hai
Mock ka type asli se drift ho sakta hai agar as any use kiya
Deep partial types likhna painful hai nested objects ke liye
gotchas: {} as User se bacho — required field add hote hi test jhooth bolne lagega
vi.mock hoist hota hai file ke top pe, isliye uske andar upar wale variables use nahi kar sakte
vi.mocked sirf type cast hai — asli mocking vi.mock karta hai

lessons.name: Testing Patterns for TypeScript Projects
lessons.desc: Organizing tests alongside source (co-located), testing type exports, snapshot testing for complex types, and integration testing with tsx/ts-node.
lessons.q: What are best practices for organizing TypeScript tests? Should you co-locate test files? How do you test that a library exports the correct public types?
lessons.qsub: What is the pattern for testing complex mapped or conditional types? How do you write a test that a type produces never for invalid inputs and a concrete type for valid inputs?
terms: mock/stub/spy — asli cheez ki jagah rakhne wali koi bhi nakli cheez
lessons.what: Definition: TypeScript projects mein test likhne ke wo tareeke jo types ka fayda uthate hain — typed factories, exhaustive case testing (satisfies se), aur type-safe it.each tables.
lessons.why: JS mein test table mein ek case bhoolna silent hai. TS mein agar table ko satisfies Record<Status, Case> likh do, to naya status add karte hi compiler chillayega ki uska test nahi hai. Coverage tool ke bina hi coverage guarantee.
where: har action type ka case cover hua ya nahi
pros: satisfies se test coverage compiler-enforced ho jaati hai
Factory + AAA se test padhne mein aasan rehte hain
it.each se duplicate test code khatam
cons: Table pattern har test ke liye fit nahi — kabhi kabhi seedha test better hai
Object.entries key ko string bana deta hai, cast karna padta hai
Zyada abstraction se test file khud debug karni padti hai
gotchas: satisfies use karo, : Record<...> annotation nahi — warna literal types chale jaayenge
Test ka naam behaviour batana chahiye, function ka naam nahi ("total jodta hai" not "test total")
Ek test mein ek hi cheez assert karo — fail hone par turant pata chale kya toota

lessons.name: Migrating JS to TypeScript
lessons.desc: Incremental migration strategies: allowJs + checkJs, @ts-check in JSDoc, max tsconfig strictness gradually, module-by-module conversion using allowJs. The "biting the apple" vs "strangler fig" approaches.
lessons.q: What is the recommended incremental migration strategy from JS to TypeScript? How does @ts-check + JSDoc annotations help in the intermediate phase?
lessons.qsub: What is the order of converting files in a monorepo migration? What are the common pain points: third-party types, dynamic require, CommonJS vs ESM, and complex generics in JS?
terms: tsconfig flag jo .js aur .ts dono ko ek saath rehne deta hai
JS files ko bhi type-check karo — JSDoc comments padhega
purani cheez ko dheere dheere nayi se replace karna, ek jhatke mein nahi
lessons.what: Definition: JS project ko TS mein le jaana — file-by-file, ek saath nahi. allowJs: true lagao, dono type ki files coexist karne do, aur leaf files (jinpe kuch depend nahi karta) se shuru karo.
lessons.analogy: Purana ghar renovate karna — sab dhaakar naya nahi banate. Ek kamra karte ho, usme rehne lagte ho, phir agla. Ghar poore time rehne layak rehta hai.
lessons.why: "Sab ek weekend mein convert kar denge" migration hamesha fail hoti hai — 400 files, 3000 type errors, koi feature ship nahi hota, team wapas JS pe chali jaati hai. Incremental mein har din code chalti halat mein rehta hai.

ek package pehle TS mein, baaki JS
log seekhte jaate hain, code migrate hota jaata hai

Team dheere dheere TS seekhti hai

Do styles ek saath — kuch confusion hoti hai

any temporary hai — TODO comment ke saath likho aur track karo, warna permanent ban jaata hai

lessons.name: Strict Mode Migration
lessons.desc: Enabling all strict flags on an existing codebase requires systematic fixes: strictNullChecks is the hardest. Use noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes incrementally.
lessons.q: How do you migrate a large codebase to strict mode? What is the correct order to enable the 8 strict flags? Which flag typically causes the most errors?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between turning on strict vs individual strict flags? When would you enable all strict flags at once vs one-by-one? How do you use @ts-expect-error as a migration tool?
terms: ek flag jo 8 alag safety flags ek saath on karta hai
null/undefined ko alag type maano — sabse bada aur sabse zaroori flag
error count sirf ghat sakta hai, badh nahi sakta — CI mein enforce karo
lessons.what: Definition: Strict mode ko ek saath on karne ki jagah, uske sub-flags ko ek-ek karke on karna. strict: true = 8 flags. Har flag alag se on karo, fix karo, commit karo.
lessons.why: Bade codebase mein strict: true daalte hi 2000+ errors aate hain. Team dekh ke haar maan leti hai aur flag wapas off ho jaata hai. Ek flag = 100-200 errors = ek din ka kaam = shippable PR.
where: jo strict:false pe likha gaya tha
JS se TS aane ke baad agla step
error count ratchet — badhne mat do
pros: Har flag ka PR chhota aur review-able hota hai
strictNullChecks akele hi sabse zyada production bugs pakadta hai
Progress dikhta hai — team ka morale banta hai
cons: Poora process hafton chal sakta hai
Beech mein naya code purane loose style mein likha jaa sakta hai
Kuch third-party types strict mode mein tootte hain
gotchas: strictNullChecks sabse aakhir mein karo — sabse zyada error deta hai
! (non-null assertion) shortcut hai, fix nahi — sirf tab jab sach mein guarantee ho
CI mein error count file mein likho aur compare karo, warna naya code errors add karta rahega

lessons.name: Types Strategy for Libraries
lessons.desc: Library authors must ship .d.ts files alongside JS. Dual CJS/ESM packages need package.json exports with types conditions. The "declaration strategy" affects consumer experience.
lessons.q: How should a TypeScript library author set up their package.json exports to support both CJS and ESM consumers with correct types?
lessons.qsub: What is the "types" condition in the exports map? How do you handle the "dual-package hazard" where a consumer accidentally gets two incompatible copies of types? What is the recommended folder structure for declaration files?
terms: declaration file — sirf types, koi code nahi
library ke wo types jo user ko dikhte hain
lessons.what: Definition: Library banate waqt types kaise ship karo. Teen tarike: (1) TS mein likho aur declaration: true se .d.ts generate karo — best; (2) JS mein likho aur haath se .d.ts likho; (3) @types/your-lib DefinitelyTyped par publish karo — sirf jab library khud JS ho aur tum author na ho.
lessons.why: Types library ka public contract hain. Agar tumne galti se ek internal type export kar diya, to use badalna breaking change ban jaata hai. Isliye jaan-boojh ke decide karo ki kya export hoga.
where: team ke doosre packages ke liye
apne repo mein local .d.ts likh ke gap bharna
pros: declaration:true se types hamesha code ke saath sync rehte hain
declarationMap se user ko asli source dikhta hai — debugging aasan
Chhota public surface = kam breaking changes
cons: Generated .d.ts kabhi kabhi bahut verbose/leaky hote hain
Dual ESM/CJS setup mein "types" order galat ho to silently fail
Har public type ab semver ka hissa hai — badalna mehnga
gotchas: exports map mein "types" sabse pehli key honi chahiye — warna resolve nahi hoti
Internal type accidentally export ho gaya to wo forever public hai
are-the-types-wrong (attw) CLI chalao publish se pehle — ye common galtiyan pakadta hai

lessons.name: TypeScript Ecosystem & Tooling
lessons.desc: ts-node, tsx, esbuild, swc, tsup, ts-morph, TypeScript ESLint, typescript-json-schema. Each tool has different TypeScript compatibility and use cases.
lessons.q: Compare ts-node, tsx, esbuild, and swc for running TypeScript files. When would you use each? What are their TypeScript fidelity differences?
lessons.qsub: What is tsup and how does it simplify library building? How does @typescript-eslint integrate with TypeScript's parser? What is tsmorph and what can it do that regex-based code mods cannot?
terms: lint rules jo types padh ke decide karti hain (slow par powerful)
esbuild/swc/rollup — build karta hai par type-check nahi karta
lessons.what:
Definition: TS ke aas-paas ke tools — typescript-eslint (linting), tsx/ts-node (seedha chalane ke liye), tsup/esbuild (build), zod (runtime validation), attw (published types check).

Sabse important samajh: bundler type-check nahi karta. Build pass hona type-safe hone ka matlab nahi.
lessons.why: Naye projects mein log Vite/esbuild use karte hain jo super fast hain kyunki wo types ko sirf hata dete hain, check nahi karte. Agar CI mein alag se tsc --noEmit nahi hai, to type errors production tak pahunch jaayenge aur kisi ko pata bhi nahi chalega.
where: typecheck + lint + test teeno alag steps
zod/valibot se incoming data validate karo
tsx script.ts se bina build kiye TS chalao
pros: zod se ek hi jagah se runtime validation + static type dono mil jaate hain
Type-aware ESLint floating promises, unsafe any jaise bugs pakadta hai
tsx se local scripts turant chal jaate hain
cons: Type-aware linting kaafi slow hai bade repo mein
Bahut saare tools = bahut saare config files
zod schemas duplicate lagte hain agar type already likha ho
gotchas: Vite/esbuild build pass hona type-safe ka proof nahi — tsc --noEmit alag chalao
API se aaya data ka type sirf ek jhooth hai jab tak runtime validate na karo
ESLint aur tsc dono ka kaam alag hai — dono chahiye, ek doosre ka replacement nahi

lessons.name: TC39 Decorators — stage 3 proposal, decorator factories
lessons.desc: Decorators are functions that modify classes, methods, properties, or parameters. TC39 Stage 3 decorators (TS 5.0+) replace the legacy experimental decorators. A decorator receives (target, context) and returns a modified value.
lessons.q: What is a TypeScript decorator? How do TC39 decorators differ from legacy experimental decorators?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between class decorators and method decorators? What is a decorator factory and why is it useful?
terms: ek function jo class/method ke upar @ lagakar uska behaviour badal deta hai
function jo decorator return karta hai — taaki argument le sako
TC39 proposal ka wo level jahan syntax final ho gaya hai — TS 5.0+ mein native
lessons.what:
Definition: Decorator ek function hai jo declaration (class, method, field, getter) ke upar @name likhne se us declaration ko wrap/modify kar deta hai — bina uska code chhue.

Do versions hain: legacy (experimentalDecorators: true, Angular/NestJS use karte hain) aur TC39 stage 3 (TS 5.0+ mein default, alag signature). Dono mix nahi hote.
lessons.analogy: Gift wrapping. Gift wahi hai, par upar se ek layer chadha di — ribbon, tag, kuch bhi. Kholne wala pehle wrapper se guzarta hai, phir gift tak pahunchta hai.
lessons.why: Cross-cutting concerns — logging, timing, caching, validation — har method mein copy-paste karne padte hain. Decorator se wo logic ek jagah likho, aur @log lagakar 20 methods pe laga do.

lessons.name: Class Decorators — modifying class behavior
lessons.desc: Class decorators receive the class constructor and can modify, replace, or wrap it. Common uses: sealed classes, dependency injection, auto-registration, mixin support.
lessons.q: How do you write a class decorator that prevents a class from being extended?
lessons.qsub: How do you use class decorators for dependency injection? What is the difference between returning a value and void from a class decorator?
terms: decorator jo poori class par lagta hai
stage-3 mein doosra argument — class ka naam, kind, addInitializer
lessons.what: Definition: Class decorator ek function hai jo class constructor leta hai aur ya to (a) kuch nahi return karta — sirf side-effect (register karna), ya (b) nayi class return karta hai jo original ko replace kar deti hai.
lessons.why: Sabse common use: registration. DI container mein class register karna, ORM ko batana ki ye class ek table hai, ya plugin system mein khud ko add karna — sab bina manual list maintain kiye.
where: @Injectable() se container ko class ka pata chalta hai
class khud ko registry mein add kar leti hai
pros: Manual registration list maintain nahi karni padti
Class ke paas hi uska metadata dikhta hai — padhne mein clear
Mixin ki tarah behaviour add kar sakte ho
cons: Return-a-new-class version mein type inference aksar tootta hai
Import na ho to registration hi nahi hoti — silent bug
Testing mushkil — global registry state carry karti hai
gotchas: Decorator tabhi chalta hai jab class module import ho — tree-shaking usse hata sakti hai
Nayi class return karne se added properties TS type mein automatically nahi aatin
Decorator class define hote hi chalta hai, instance banne pe nahi

lessons.name: Method & Property Decorators — logging, memoization, validation
lessons.desc: Method decorators intercept method calls for logging, timing, caching, or validation. Property decorators track property access. Common in frameworks like NestJS, TypeORM, and Angular.
lessons.q: How do you create a method decorator that logs execution time? How do you create a property decorator that validates values?
lessons.qsub: What is the context object in decorators (name, static, private)? How do you use decorators to implement the @sealed pattern?
terms: ek method ko wrap karta hai — signature same, behaviour extra
property par lagta hai; initializer ki value badal sakta hai
ctx ka function — instance banne par kuch chalane ke liye
lessons.what:
Definition: Method decorator asli method leta hai aur naya function return karta hai jo usko wrap karta hai. Field/getter decorators bhi isi tarah kaam karte hain par unka signature alag hai.

Practical uses: memoize, debounce, retry, timing, permission-check, deprecation warning.
lessons.why: Memoization ka logic 5 lines ka hai. Us 5 line ko 10 alag methods mein copy karne ki jagah ek @memo decorator likho. Logic ek jagah — bug fix bhi ek jagah.
pros: Same logic 10 methods pe ek line mein
Method ka apna code bilkul saaf rehta hai
Signature same rehta hai to callers ko pata bhi nahi chalta
cons: this ka type sambhalna padta hai warna galti se global this
Async methods ke liye wrapper alag likhna padta hai
Cache leak ho sakta hai agar WeakMap ki jagah Map use kiya
gotchas: Method ka `this` bind rakho — target.apply(this, args), seedha target(...args) nahi
Cache instance-wise rakho (WeakMap), warna do objects ka data mix ho jaayega
Field decorator ka return ek initializer FUNCTION hota hai, value nahi

lessons.name: Decorator Composition — ordering, combining multiple decorators
lessons.desc: Multiple decorators compose bottom-to-top (inner decorator runs first). Decorator factories return functions, enabling parameterization. NestJS uses this heavily for @Controller, @Injectable, @Get.
lessons.q: How do decorators compose? What is the execution order when you apply multiple decorators to a single method?
lessons.qsub: How does NestJS use decorators for route definition? What is the difference between @Controller and @Injectable decorators?
terms: ek hi cheez par kai decorators lagana
sabse neeche wala decorator pehle apply hota hai
sabse upar wala — call ke waqt sabse pehle chalta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Ek method/class par kai decorators lagana. Do alag order hote hain aur yahi interview ka favourite sawaal hai:

  • Apply order — neeche se upar (bottom-up). Sabse neeche wala pehle wrap karta hai.
  • Execution order — call ke waqt upar se neeche. Sabse upar wala outermost layer hai.

Factories alag hain: @log(1) @log(2) mein factory calls upar se neeche hoti hain, phir apply neeche se upar.
lessons.analogy: Pyaaz ki layers. Chhilte waqt (apply) andar se bahar lagti gayi thi; kaatte waqt (call) bahar wali pehle milti hai.
lessons.why: Order galat samjhe to bug pakad mein nahi aata: @cache @auth mein cache pehle chalega — matlab unauthorized user ko cached result mil sakta hai! @auth @cache sahi hai — pehle auth check, phir cache.
